--- > **See it live:** **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. > No install required; the interface loads immediately, while live data, chat, and > mutations need the local sidecar ([Deployment](docs/deployment.md)). To run the > full stack yourself, jump to [Quick Start](#quick-start). **Agentic ODI** explores how the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server acts as the "brain" of customer needs — letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in verified, measurable customer outcomes (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores). This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. **Project site:** the static page lives at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)** and is republished by the `Pages` workflow on every push to `main`. **Hosted Studio:** the experimental Living Studio UI runs at **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. It loads without a backend; live data needs the sidecar tunnel described in [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers Builds. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) with shared tooling at the root. Packages live in `packages/`, runnable services in `apps/`, and deployment assets in `infra/`: | Path | Distribution | Description | |---|---|---| | **`packages/core/`** | `agentic-odi-core` | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), the shared MCP tool contract, and ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`packages/connectors/`** | `agentic-odi-connectors` | Pluggable MCP and REST connectors with presets and an ingest sink. | | **`apps/mcp-server/`** | `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | FastMCP server exposing Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, Evidence, and context tools over HTTP. Persists to SQLite by default. | | **`apps/studio-api/`** | `agentic-odi-studio-api` | FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. Serves config, health, canvas data, local mutations, MCP passthrough, SSE chat, and the built SPA. | | **`apps/cli/`** | `agentic-odi-cli` | Typer CLI with interactive chat plus full entity CRUD, `schema`, `connectors`, and local-first (`--backend local`) or remote (`--backend mcp`) data access. | | **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The copilot renders **agent-composed surfaces inline** — scored outcomes, opportunity boards, bet simulations — from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** hands a new user off to the context conversation or straight to a surface. | | **`infra/cloudflare/`** | Worker | Free-plan Workers Static Assets deployment and sidecar tunnel. | | **`scripts/`** | — | Dev launcher, binary build, installer tests. | | **`tests/contract/`** | — | Cross-package MCP contract tests. | See [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) for the dependency graph, data flow, and testing strategy. ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager. ```bash # Install the entire workspace (all five Python projects plus dev tooling) uv sync --all-packages # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together npm --prefix apps/studio run build python scripts/dev.py ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | For hot reload, `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The first time you open the Studio it asks — conversationally, in the chat, and skippable at any point — for your product, audience, and the job your customers are trying to get done. Answer what you like; every reply starts from what you shared. After that it opens as one room: the transcript and the composer never leave the screen. Describe a job or a customer frustration, or type `/` for commands that mirror the CLI. Whatever the thread produces — scored outcomes, a job map, customer evidence — arrives as an inline surface, and a quiet rail above the conversation opens it in a lens that docks beside the thread instead of replacing it. Capture and simulation are conversations too: tell the studio what a customer said, or what bet you are weighing, and it renders the card. Use the bell to **catch up on outcome shifts, simulations, and telemetry signals while you were away**. The Studio is better with an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support (see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md)), but it does not depend on one: with no model reachable it says so and every job, step, and outcome remains editable by hand. ### Connectors (MCP ↔ Living Studio) Register MCP or REST connectors that the copilot can discover and invoke. - **Where they live**: a shared `connectors.json` registry. Override its location with `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`; by default it is `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`. See [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md). - **In the Living Studio**: open the **Settings** drawer → **Connectors** to list, remove, or add one of the recommended presets (Notion, PostHog, Exa, Linear, GitHub). - **Conversationally**: tell the copilot "use Notion" / "add the GitHub connector". It emits an `add_connector` local tool (handled in-process) that writes the preset to the registry, plus a `connector` SSE event the Studio surfaces as a suggestion chip. Dismissing or accepting the chip also refreshes the list. - **API**: `GET/POST/DELETE /api/connectors`, `GET /api/connectors/catalog`, and `GET /api/connectors/{name}/health` (the catalog honors `?area=` and `?recommended=true`). - **CLI**: `agentic-odi connectors catalog | add | list | health | ingest `. ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m agentic_odi_cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m agentic_odi_cli --help # show available options and commands python -m agentic_odi_cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi jobs list # Jobs-to-be-Done agentic-odi steps list --job-id agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi evidence list --job-id agentic-odi schema # canonical JSON schema for every entity agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). See the [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md). ### Install the binary Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` The installer symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`. See [Installation](docs/installation.md) for the install layout, updates, and release automation. ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | |---|---| | [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md) | Backends, interactive chat, Jobs/Steps/desired Outcomes/Customer Outcomes/evidence, `connectors`, scoring, environment variables | | [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md) | The MCP ingest connector, presets, and the `Connector` protocol | | [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md) | First-run tour and its flag, interface, rich inline responses and the UI catalog, run modes, desktop signing and updates, agent-driven testing (`/dev`, `/test`) | | [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md) | Running a local OpenAI-compatible model with tool calling | | [Development](docs/development.md) | Lint, format, type checks, frontend checks, tests and the coverage map | | [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) | Workspace layout, dependency direction, data flow, and testing | | [Installation](docs/installation.md) | Binary install, updater behavior, and release automation | | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) | Project site on GitHub Pages, Hosted Studio and PR preview URLs, the MCP server endpoint, and the free-plan Cloudflare Worker | | [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) | Completed and upcoming milestones | | [Superpowers](docs/superpowers.md) | Pi, OpenCode, and Freebuff integration | ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! This project uses [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) for linting and formatting and [pytest](https://pytest.org/) for tests. Make sure your change passes the [lint, format, and test checks](docs/development.md) before opening a pull request. ## License This project is licensed under the terms of the MIT License — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details. ---

<skill_content name="brainstorming">
# Skill: brainstorming

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Questions that work** anchor in specifics: "Walk me through the last
time...", "If it could only do one of these well, which?", "What would
make you wince if I got it wrong?" A guess they can correct ("I'm
guessing this is because X keeps biting you?") often beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking would help,
offer to go look: their codebase or project, their own files and data,
or the web. Say what you'd look for. They decide whether you go.

**Think wide privately.** Before you propose anything, come up with
several ideas and drop the weak ones, including any that fight what
they've told you about why. Show the comparison only when it helps them
decide.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Mark anything you're guessing as your guess; only what they said goes in
as theirs. End each chunk by asking what's wrong or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want, pick a size and say it in plain
words. They can override it.

| Size | The full description | Then |
|------|----------------------|------|
| A quick, clear task | the request itself | do it |
| A small change | in chat | build it through the normal workflow |
| A project with a written design | a written design document | a full plan (for software: superpowers:writing-plans) |

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

For a project, write a plain document a talented builder in the domain
could plan from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.

**Builder check:** dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

<HARD-GATE>
Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the full
description: in chat for a small change, the document for a project.
Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After a project's document is approved, the next step is the plan. For
software, invoke superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
</HARD-GATE>

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I'll offer options to save them effort" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
| "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |
| "I should explain the process first" | Ask your question. The process shows itself. |
| "They said 'sounds good' to the idea" | Approval covers what you showed them. A description you haven't written isn't approved. |
| "The spike works, I'll keep building on it" | Keeping it is a new request. Back through the gate. |

## Visual Companion

A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
browser.

**Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
else in it:

> "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"

If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.

If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
starting the server.

**Global resets:** `* { box-sizing: border-box }`; `html, body, #root { height: 100% }`; `body { margin: 0; -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased }`; `button { -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent }`; `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px }`; `.sr-only` utility; custom `::-webkit-scrollbar` (8px, `rgba(255,255,255,0.15)` thumb, `rgba(0,0,0,0.2)` track, 4px radius).

### 1e. The file's layered history (important for the marketing site)

`theme.css` is a palimpsest of four generations appended chronologically:

1. **Lines 1–1440** — the original hand-crafted system (`--bg`, `--accent`, `--faint`, `.chat`, `.composer`, `.card`, `.badge`, `.metric`).
2. **Lines 1442–1613** — "Manual data controls" + bell/catch-up.
3. **Lines 1614–2407** — the "Generated surfaces" block (`.ui-*`), which is the **Tailwind-slate-flavoured** generation.
4. **Lines 2409–2608** — Changelog modal ("Steve Jobs Quality").
5. **Lines 2610–2809** — "PR #61 micro-interactions" — the Apple-glass generation, adding the `--ease-*` tokens.
6. **Lines 2810–3094** — "One room: the conversation never leaves the stage" — the **Rail + Lens** generation.

  font-size: 0.82rem;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: background 0.14s ease;
}

.button:hover:not(:disabled) {
  background: rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.26);
}

.button:disabled {
  opacity: 0.45;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}

.button--ghost {
  border-color: var(--line);
  background: transparent;
}

.button--ghost:hover:not(:disabled) {
  background: var(--surface-hover);
}

.button--block {
  width: 100%;
}

.disclosure {
  padding-top: 6px;
  border-top: 1px solid var(--line);
  color: var(--muted);
  font-size: 0.8rem;
}

.disclosure summary {
  cursor: pointer;
  color: var(--muted);
  font-size: 0.78rem;
  list-style: none;
}

.disclosure summary::-webkit-details-marker {
  display: none;
}

.disclosure summary::before {
  content: "+ ";
  color: var(--faint);
}

.disclosure[open] summary::before {
  content: "− ";
}

.disclosure > * + * {
  margin-top: 10px;
}

.disclosure p {
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.76rem;
  line-height: 1.55;
}

/* Impact */
.before-after {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
  gap: 8px;
}

.compare {
  padding: 11px 12px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 12px;
  font-size: 0.76rem;
}

.compare--before {
  border-color: rgba(248, 113, 113, 0.2);
  background: rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.06);
}

.compare--after {
  border-color: rgba(74, 222, 128, 0.2);
  background: rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.06);
}

.compare__label {
  display: block;
  margin-bottom: 6px;
  font-size: 0.63rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.1em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--faint);
}

.compare ul {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 5px;
  margin: 0;
  padding-left: 15px;
  color: var(--muted);
  line-height: 1.45;
}

.compare b {
  color: var(--text);
  font-weight: 600;
}

.score-preview {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: 8px;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 10px 12px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 10px;

  font-size: 0.95rem;

  margin: 0;

  border-radius: 10px;

  color: #d6c19b;
  font-size: 0.74rem;
  line-height: 1.5;

Your roadmap is a guess.

Agentic ODI Run it in 60 seconds

Opinion is expensive.

"Roadmaps set by whoever talks loudest." — Decisions default to seniority, not evidence.
"Features for customers who never asked." — Nobody validated the outcome; only the idea.
"Agents fluent in everything, grounded in nothing." — A model will confidently invent your customer.

Add it up and the roadmap isn't a plan. It's a guess.

Ask for outcomes, not opinions.

Outcome-Driven Innovation asks customers how much each desired outcome matters and how satisfied they are with it today.

The gap between importance and satisfaction is where products win or die.

Agentic ODI stores those outcomes, scores them, and serves them to any agent over MCP.

Opportunity = Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)

86% innovation success rate — as reported in ODI literature (Strategyn)

How it works.

  1. Capture — jobs, steps, and desired outcomes with importance/satisfaction scores, via CLI, connectors, or The Living Studio.
  2. Query — agents call MCP tools for job maps and opportunity scores at decision time, local or hosted.
  3. Steer — The Living Studio shows the Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, and Impact Simulation so the team decides from the same picture.

Run it in 60 seconds.

cd agentic-odi

Now I have a complete picture. Let me summarize what I found and then ask the user the key questions.

**Current state:**
- Live site: bare 5-section text page, `alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/`
- Single column, 64ch, placeholder SVG "illustrative" figures instead of product shots
- 3 conflicting color palettes; inline hardcoded colors break dark mode
- Title "Agentic ODI — Agentic ODI"; description truncated mid-sentence
- h1 above the header
- Copy button broken (`.copy_btn` vs `.copy-btn`); `.revealed` class undefined
- Generated by `sync-readme.py` (a Python string-literal template) — must be rewritten
- `make_og.py` generates og.png/favicon.png deterministically; tests assert pixel-identity
- 5 test files encode a "site contract" — must be updated
- Deploy: `.github/workflows/pages.yml` → rsync `website/` → `_site/`, gated on `uv run --directory website pytest tests/`

**Product reality (way ahead of the site):**
- Living Studio: React 19 + Vite + Tauri 2 desktop app
- Chat-first "one room" UX with Rail + Lens
- 30 MCP tools (jobs, steps, outcomes, customer outcomes, evidence, opportunity scoring, ODI schema, framework guidelines, capabilities, promote_evidence, evaluate_outcome)
- Agent-composed surfaces: 9 primitives + 6 ODI cards (outcome-card, opportunity-board, impact-simulation, evidence-quote, job-map, decision-record)
- 17 connector presets (Notion, Gong, Fireflies, Intercom, Confluence, PostHog, Amplitude, Mixpanel, Exa, Tavily, Linear, GitHub, Jira, Miro, Figma, Slack)
- CLI: local-first, interactive chat, entity CRUD, `schema`, `score`, `connectors`
- Prebuilt binaries (Linux/macOS/Windows) via install.sh
- Hosted Studio on Cloudflare Workers + PR previews
- First-run wizard, feature flags, changelog drawer, catch-up notifications
- Design system: dark-first, indigo #8b8cf8 / #6366f1, bg #0a0b0e, Apple easings, glassmorphism

**Key design decisions to confirm with user:**

1. **Build architecture** — Options:
   - (A) Keep zero-build static HTML/CSS/JS (rsync). Pros: no npm, matches current CI, no supply chain, tests stay simple. Cons: harder to achieve Apple-level polish at scale; multi-page means hand-written repetition.
   - (B) Astro static site build. Pros: component reuse, multi-page easy, islands for interactivity, excellent a11y/perf. Cons: adds npm build step to Pages CI, new dependency.
   - (C) Vite + React (same stack as Studio) — full reuse of the Studio design language/components, but heaviest.

   Given the Studio already has React/Vite/TypeScript, and the site needs to feel like the product, and needs a real "product showcase" — Astro is a strong middle ground. But the repo's CI is Python-centric and the site has a "no npm" heritage. Let me recommend Astro.

2. **Scope: single page or multi-page?** "Any and all details" suggests multi-page: landing + docs hub + architecture. Or one long-scroll landing with a docs section. Let me ask.

3. **Product visuals** — No screenshots exist. Options: (a) capture real screenshots by running the Studio (needs the app running + a browser); (b) hand-craft pixel-accurate HTML/CSS recreations of the Studio UI as "device frames" (Apple-style, honest if labeled as UI recreation); (c) both.

4. **Audience/positioning** — Dev-first (MCP/CLI/agents) vs PM-first (outcomes/strategy) vs both. The hero currently is "Your roadmap is a guess." which is PM-facing. The actual product is very dev-facing (MCP server, 30 tools, connectors).

5. **Dark-only vs dual theme?** Studio is dark-only (`color-scheme: dark`). Apple.com is dual. A state-of-the-art site should do dual theme (the current CSS tries). But the product is dark-first. Let me ask, or recommend dark-first with light fallback. Actually — the site is "the window to the world" and the product is a dark-only app. I'd recommend: dark-first, with a real light theme too, since the current site advertises light and the OG card is dark. Hmm, but OG art is dark. Apple-quality = full dark primary.

Let me also consider: the "honesty contract" tests. Those are deliberate product stance — I should preserve them but they need updating as content changes.

Let me now formulate my questions. Per brainstorming skill: first message should be one line offering to skip questions + one open question. But I've already done a lot of exploration. Let me present findings concisely and ask focused questions. I'll use the `question` tool for a structured choice on the biggest tradeoffs.

Actually, the brainstorming skill says ask one open question per message. But the `question` tool supports multiple. Let me be pragmatic and respectful of the user's time: I'll present the key findings, then ask the 3-4 decisive questions via the question tool.

Let me first check one more critical thing: is there a design doc for the original GitHub Pages (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-github-pages-design.md)? That tells me the original intent and constraints. And the deployment doc. Let me read those quickly — they're important for constraints.

Let me also verify the current test suite passes / what the exact test contract is, since that's the gate.

Let me read the github-pages design spec + deployment doc.
Let me read the original Pages design spec and deployment doc — they encode constraints I must respect.

# GitHub Pages Marketing Site Design

**Date:** 2026-10-18
**Status:** Approved (design authority delegated to the session designer; all builder-check questions answered)
**Scope:** Single-page customer-facing site in `website/` + GitHub Actions deploy to GitHub Pages

## Intent & Why

`README.md` is the project's front door, and it reads like an engineering changelog — right for
contributors, wrong for the PM or eng lead who clicked a shared link asking "is this real, and is it
worth five minutes?" The site answers why/what/how/when in one scroll, with a Jobsian bar:
ruthless focus, one narrative, one obvious action, craft in type and motion, and honesty as the
brand — the project is an experimental testbed, and the page says so out loud.

The Jobsian constraint that shapes everything: **over-promising on an experimental product is the
one thing Jobs never did — the honest answer is the Jobsian answer.** No dates, no maturity theater,
no CTAs that dead-end behind auth, no screenshots of vaporware.

Definition of done for the build (see plan): PR pushed with all GitHub Actions checks green —
lint (ruff), typecheck (mypy), security (bandit), tests (pytest ×6 packages + `website`), smoke,
and the "CI green" aggregate.

## Audience & Jobs-to-be-Done

**Primary — product managers / innovation leads.** Landing cold from a shared link, a search, or a
referral. Skeptical of AI-tool marketing.
> When I open this page from a link in Slack, I want to know within one screen whether this is a
> real, runnable thing grounded in a method I respect, so I can decide to spend five minutes on it
> or leave without guilt.

**Secondary — AI/agent developers.** Evaluating whether to wire agents to an ODI data source.
> When I'm deciding what context to give my agents, I want the exact endpoint and a copy-paste
> quickstart that works locally, so I can try it without talking to anyone.

**Tertiary — the sharing PM (internal champion).** Forwarding the link to a team or a boss.
> When I forward this page, I want it to frame the thesis — evidence over opinion — credibly and
> soberly, so the conversation starts from the idea instead of from my credibility.

## Messaging Hierarchy

Binding copy contract (tests enforce the marked strings; micro-polish — punctuation-level tweaks —
is builder latitude).

| Level | Copy |
|---|---|
| Eyebrow pill | `Experimental` |
| H1 (hero) | **Your roadmap is a guess.** |
| Hero sub | An MCP server that hands your agents verified customer outcomes — and the evidence behind them. |
| Primary CTA | **Run it in 60 seconds** → `#run` (local quickstart) |
| Secondary CTA | View on GitHub → `https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi` |
| Tertiary link | Hosted demo — requires a free Prefect account → Horizon chat URL |
| Footer tagline | Built with outcomes, not guesses. |

**Section 2 — `#problem`, "Opinion is expensive."** Three parallel beats, one line each, each with
a short support line:

1. "Roadmaps set by whoever talks loudest." — Decisions default to seniority, not evidence.
2. "Features for customers who never asked." — Nobody validated the outcome; only the idea.
3. "Agents fluent in everything, grounded in nothing." — A model will confidently invent your customer.

Section closer: "Add it up and the roadmap isn't a plan. It's a guess."

**Section 3 — `#insight`, "Ask for outcomes, not opinions."** Three plain sentences:
1. Outcome-Driven Innovation asks customers how much each desired outcome matters and how satisfied
   they are with it today.
2. The gap between importance and satisfaction is where products win or die.
3. Agentic ODI stores those outcomes, scores them, and serves them to any agent over MCP.

Then: a small CSS/inline-SVG bar visual (Importance vs Satisfaction, gap highlighted, labeled
"Illustrative outcome data"), the formula rendered exactly as the code computes it —
`Opportunity = Importance + max(Importance − Satisfaction, 0)` (source of truth:
`core/src/core/models.py:27`), and the stat callout: **86%** innovation success rate — *as reported
in ODI literature (Strategyn)*. Plain-text attribution only; no link to the in-repo PDF.

**Section 4 — `#how`, "How it works."** Three steps:
1. **Capture** — jobs, steps, and desired outcomes with importance/satisfaction scores, via CLI,
   connectors, or The Living Studio.
2. **Query** — agents call MCP tools for job maps and opportunity scores at decision time, local or
   hosted.
3. **Steer** — The Living Studio shows the Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, and Impact
   Simulation so the team decides from the same picture.

Accompanies: a stylized Studio illustration (real shipped surfaces, marked "Illustrative"), never a
fake screenshot.

**Section 5 — `#run`, "Run it in 60 seconds."** Prerequisites line (Python 3.10+, uv), terminal
block with copy button:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi.git
cd agentic-odi
uv sync --all-packages
python -m client.run
```

Endpoint chips with copy buttons: MCP `http://localhost:8000/mcp` · Studio `http://localhost:8501`.
MCP client config snippet (local only):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "agentic-odi": { "url": "http://localhost:8000/mcp" }
  }
}
```

Prose note: hosted credentials come from the maintainers — open an issue. Never invent an auth
scheme we cannot document.

**Section 6 — `#status`, "Honest status."** `Experimental` badge; **What works today** (MCP server
tools for jobs/steps/outcomes/customer outcomes with opportunity scoring; The Living Studio —
Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, Impact Simulation, Causal Lineage; CLI `outcomes` +
`connectors`; MCP ingest connector; hosted test endpoints requiring auth) and **What's next**
(curated from the README roadmap at build time: map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts, more
connector kinds, ODI schema definition, context tooling, persistence layer, agentic integration).
Standing line: "We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does." Closer: "Questions?
Open an issue." → Issues link.

**Footer.** Mark + wordmark, tagline, links (GitHub, Issues, Hosted demo), legal line:
`© 2026 Agentic ODI maintainers · All rights reserved` + one-line experimental reminder.

**Voice rules:** warm, direct, second person; plain language; no jargon dumps; **no emoji anywhere
on the site** (house copy rule from the first-run onboarding spec — README's emoji style stays in
README); no superlatives ("revolutionary", "seamless", "enterprise-grade"); English only.

## Information Architecture / Sitemap

| Route | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `website/index.html` | The entire site. One scroll, seven sections. |
| `/404.html` | `website/404.html` | On-brand, **self-contained** (inline styles, absolute link home) so it renders at any depth on project Pages. |

- Sticky compact header: mark + wordmark (left), single CTA "Run it in 60 seconds" (right). No nav
  links — one page needs no navigation, but the one obvious action must stay reachable.
- In-page anchors: `#problem`, `#insight`, `#how`, `#run`, `#status`.
- No sitemap.xml, no robots.txt, no blog, no docs pages, no search.

## Visual Direction

**Type.** No webfonts, zero downloads:
- `--font-sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif`
  (same stack The Living Studio ships, `client/src/client/app.py:36`)
- `--font-mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`

| Role | Size | Weight / tracking |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | `clamp(2.75rem, 6.5vw, 4.75rem)` | 700, `-0.02em`, lh 1.05 |
| H2 | `clamp(1.75rem, 3.2vw, 2.5rem)` | 700, `-0.015em`, lh 1.15 |
| H3 / beats | `1.25rem` | 600, lh 1.3 |
| Body / lead | `1.0625rem` (17px) / `1.1875rem` | 400, lh 1.6 |
| Eyebrow, badges | `0.75rem` | 600, `0.08em`, uppercase |
| Code | `0.9375rem` mono | lh 1.55 |

**Color.** Tokens as CSS custom properties; `:root` = light, `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`
overrides. Palette echoes the shipped Studio dark-glass theme (`#0B0D13` / `#131722` / `#F1F5F9`
straight from `app.py`). All ratios measured, WCAG 2.1 AA (text ≥ 4.5:1):

| Token | Light | Dark | Contrast (light / dark) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--bg` | `#ffffff` | `#0b0d13` | — |
| `--surface` | `#f5f5f7` | `#131722` | — |
| `--text` | `#1d1d1f` | `#f1f5f9` | 16.8 on bg / 17.7 on bg |
| `--muted` | `#6e6e73` | `#94a3b8` | 5.07 bg, 4.66 surface / 7.58 bg, 6.98 surface |
| `--accent` (button fill, white label) | `#0071e3` | `#0071e3` | white on it: 4.70 (both) |
| `--accent-text` (link text) | `#0062c4` | `#409cff` | 5.93 bg, 5.44 surface / 6.86 bg, 6.32 surface |
| `--accent-hover` | `#0059b8` | `#0059b8` | white on it: 6.73 |
| `--badge` (fg on bg) | `#475569` on `#e2e8f0` | `#cbd5e1` on `#1e293b` | 6.15 / 9.85 |
| `--border` | `rgba(0,0,0,.08)` | `rgba(148,163,184,.16)` | decorative only |

Code blocks are dark (`#0b0d13`) in both schemes — a terminal is a terminal (17.7:1 either way).
OG card is fixed dark, self-contained.

**Layout & spacing.** Mobile-first; content max-width 1080px, prose max-width 68ch; inline padding
`clamp(20px, 5vw, 40px)`; section padding-block `clamp(72px, 12vw, 140px)`; 8px spacing scale as
custom properties; radius 12px cards / 999px pills (echoing the Studio's own radii); 1px hairline
borders. Beats and steps go two-column at ≥720px.

**Motion.** Restrained, explanatory, never load-bearing:
- Hero stagger on load: eyebrow → H1 → sub → CTAs, 12px fade-up, 60ms stagger, 400ms,
  `cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)` — pure CSS, no JS.
- Scroll reveal: sections fade-up once when 15% visible (IntersectionObserver). Default state is
  **visible**; JS opts content into the hidden-then-reveal state only after it loads, so no-JS
  readers never see hidden content.
- Buttons: 150ms `background-color`/`transform`, hover `translateY(-1px)`, active `scale(.98)`.
- Copy button swaps its label to "Copied" for 1.5s, announced via an `aria-live="polite"` span.
- `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`: all transforms/stagger removed, reveals off, content
  immediate.

**Imagery & assets (none exist in the repo — all created):**
- **Mark** (`mark.svg`, hand-authored, viewBox `0 0 32 32`): rounded-square canvas with an
  ascending two-step polyline and a filled dot at the apex — the opportunity curve breaking
  upward. Accent stroke `#0071e3`, hairline frame. Works at 16px, single color-safe.
- **Favicon:** `favicon.svg` (same geometry) + `favicon.png` 32×32 (generated, dark tile, for
  browsers that ignore SVG icons).
- **Opportunity visual:** pure CSS/inline SVG bars in `#insight`, `aria`-labeled, marked
  "Illustrative outcome data".
- **Studio illustration:** stylized abstraction of shipped surfaces only (Opportunity Landscape,
  Universal Job Map, Impact Simulation — verified in `client/src/client/app.py:683-838`), marked
  "Illustrative". Depicting vaporware on a page whose thesis is "no guesses" would self-destruct.
- All decorative SVGs `aria-hidden="true"`; no stock photos, no icon fonts, no emoji.

## Content Sources

| Content | Source | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| Quickstart commands (`uv sync --all-packages`, `python -m client.run`) | README §Getting Started — **verbatim** | `test_readme_sync.py` |
| Local endpoints (`http://localhost:8000/mcp`, `http://localhost:8501`) | README One-Command Launch — **verbatim** | `test_readme_sync.py` |
| Hosted chat URL | README §Deployment — **verbatim**; the label "requires a free Prefect account" is fresh | `test_readme_sync.py` + allowlist |
| Experimental framing, maturity claims | README banner — adapted, no new claims | review + honesty tests |
| What works today / What's next | README roadmap checkboxes, curated at build time (re-read README in Task 2 of the plan) | review focus |
| License/legal line | README §License — adapted ("All rights reserved") | honesty test |
| 86% stat + "as reported in ODI literature (Strategyn)" | Session decision (no link to `knowledge/*.pdf`) | honesty test |
| Opportunity formula | `core/src/core/models.py:27-29` | formula test |
| Headline, subhead, beats, section titles, CTA labels, tagline, OG copy | **Written fresh** — binding in this spec | structural tests |
| Mark, favicon, illustrations, OG art | Created per this spec | asset tests |

Rule: README is the source of truth for every command, URL, and status claim. If the page and
README disagree, the page is wrong.

## Technical Approach

Hand-crafted static HTML + one CSS file + ≤100 lines of vanilla JS. **No framework** (no
Astro/Next/React): one page with no routing, no state, no data, no components shared across
views — a framework buys a toolchain, a lockfile, hydration, and an upgrade treadmill, and charges
rent on every one of them. Consequence of no framework: deploy is "copy files", the review diff is
readable HTML, Lighthouse is high by construction, and there is zero supply chain on the page.

```
website/
  index.html            # the site
  404.html              # self-contained fallback
  assets/
    style.css           # tokens + full design system (no external URLs)
    main.js             # ≤100 lines: reveal + copy buttons, defer, progressive enhancement
    mark.svg  favicon.svg
    og.png    favicon.png   # committed, generated (see OG strategy)
  tools/
    make_og.py          # regenerates og.png + favicon.png (Pillow, pinned)
  tests/
    test_site.py  test_assets.py  test_make_og.py
    test_workflows.py  test_readme_sync.py
```

- **Paths:** every in-page URL is **relative** (`assets/…`, `#anchor`) so the site works under the
  project-Pages base `/agentic-odi/`, on a local static server, and on any future custom domain.
  `og:url` / `og:image` / `rel=canonical` are **absolute**.
- Local preview: `python3 -m http.server 8080 --directory website` (preview the 404 by opening
  `/404.html` directly — `http.server` serves its own 404).
- JS is `defer`'d and additive: the page is complete, styled, and readable with JS disabled.
- Python tooling lives only in `tools/` + `tests/`, run from the repo root with the workspace venv.

## OG / Social Strategy

Social previews are the main earned-distribution artifact — one committed raster, no mystery binary.

- `website/assets/og.png`: **1200×630**, fixed dark card — mark + "Agentic ODI" wordmark,
  headline "Your roadmap is a guess.", sub "Verified customer outcomes, jobs, and opportunity
  scores — served over MCP.", bottom row `alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi` + Experimental badge.
- `website/tools/make_og.py`: the committed, runnable generator (stdlib argparse + Pillow). Writes
  `og.png` and `favicon.png`; defaults embed the canonical card copy above. Deterministic output —
  fixed palette/positions, no timestamps, `compress_level=9`, font via
  `ImageFont.load_default(size=…)` (Pillow's embedded Aileron, SIL OFL — no font file in the repo).
  Run: `uv run python website/tools/make_og.py`.
- **Regenerability is enforced:** `test_make_og.py` renders fresh bytes and asserts they are
  pixel-identical to the committed PNGs. Change the script → the test fails until you regenerate.
  Change the card copy → defaults in the script are the source.
- Meta contract on `index.html`: `og:type=website`, `og:site_name`, `og:title`
  ("Your roadmap is a guess. — Agentic ODI"), `og:description`, `og:url` (canonical Pages URL),
  `og:image` (absolute PNG URL), `twitter:card=summary_large_image` + title/description/image,
  `rel=canonical`, `theme-color` per color scheme, both favicons. Title tag ≤ 60 chars:
  `Agentic ODI — Ground agents in verified customer outcomes`.
- og:image is never loaded by the page itself (page weight unaffected).
- No OpenGraph on SVG: scrapers (X, LinkedIn, Slack, iMessage) need raster — hence exactly one PNG.

## Deploy Pipeline

**`.github/workflows/pages.yml`** (deploy only — its contract is tested in `ci.yml` via
`test_workflows.py`, so PRs validate it without triggering a deploy):

- `on: push branches [main] paths [website/**, .github/workflows/pages.yml]`, plus
  `workflow_dispatch`.
- Workflow permissions: `contents: read`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`. Concurrency:
  `group: pages`, `cancel-in-progress: false`. Environment: `github-pages` (URL from the
  deployment step).
- Job `deploy`, steps: checkout@v7 → `./.github/actions/setup` → **run
  `uv run pytest website/tests -q` (verify before publish)** → `actions/configure-pages@v6` →
  stage the artifact with

timeout 10m) and add `website` to `ci-green`'s `needs`. Root `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .`
already cover `website/**` once root ruff config exists (below).

## Accessibility & Performance Budget

**Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA):**
- Semantic landmarks (`header`/`main`/`footer`), one `h1`, no skipped heading levels, `lang="en"`.
- Contrast: measured pairs in the color table — every text pair ≥ 4.5:1 in both schemes.
- Full keyboard operability; visible focus ring (≥ 3:1 against adjacent colors); copy controls are
  real `<button>`s with accessible names; `aria-live` for "Copied".
- Decorative SVG `aria-hidden="true"`; meaningful links (no "click here"); `prefers-reduced-motion`
  respected; viewport meta; tested at 360px width with no horizontal scroll.

**Performance:**
- Zero third-party requests, zero webfonts, zero analytics, zero cookies — the page talks only to
  its own origin.

  ≤ 10 KB, `favicon.png` ≤ 5 KB, total transferred ≤ 150 KB; `og.png` ≤ 300 KB (test-enforced;
  expected ~15–40 KB).

  manual run before merge — CI has no browser).

- **Not a docs site, not a blog.** No MkDocs/Docusaurus, no nav maze, no search, no sitemap.
- **No framework, no build step, no dependencies on the deployed artifact.**
- **No claims the repo can't back:** no dates or milestones; no "open source" or license claim
  (repo is all-rights-reserved); no maturity language beyond the Experimental framing; no invented
  testimonials, logos, customer counts, or benchmark numbers; no emoji.
- **No dead ends:** no CTAs behind auth (hosted is tertiary, labeled); no personal emails, no
  invented Discord/Slack; access channel = GitHub Issues only.
- **No auth fiction:** local MCP config only; never link the 401 `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app`
  endpoint as something a visitor can try; no invented header/token scheme.
- **No vaporware imagery:** Studio illustration is abstraction-of-shipped-surfaces, labeled
  "Illustrative"; no fake screenshots.
- **No hotlinking `knowledge/Strategyn_*.pdf`** — attribution text only.
- **No analytics/cookies/CDN/fonts/i18n** — scope is English, one page, two schemes.
- **No publishing dev files:** `website/tests/` and `website/tools/` never reach the Pages artifact.

1. **Pages not enabled before first merge** → deploy job red on `main`. Mitigation: manual toggle
   flagged as a pre-merge gate in the plan's final task.
2. **README drift** (commands/URLs change, page rots) → `test_readme_sync.py` fails CI.
3. **Committed PNG drifts from generator** → pixel-identity test fails CI until regeneration.
4. **Scope creep** (nav items, extra pages, webfonts) → anti-goals + structural tests (allowlisted
   links, weight budgets) push back mechanically.
5. **Ruff newly covers `website/**`** → root config added at repo-consistent line length; commit
   steps run root lint/format parity before every commit.

2. **Access channel** → GitHub Issues (footer + status section). No personal email, no invented
   Discord.
3. **MCP snippet** → local config only (`http://localhost:8000/mcp`); hosted credentials are
   requested via issues. Never document an auth scheme we don't have.
4. **OG image** → one committed PNG, regenerated by committed `website/tools/make_og.py`
   (deterministic, tested pixel-identical). SVG-only cards render poorly on X/LinkedIn/iMessage.
5. **"When"** → no dates. "What works today / What's next" under an explicit Experimental badge,
   mirroring the README roadmap.
6. **Living Studio visual** → stylized abstraction grounded in real shipped surfaces, labeled
   "Illustrative" — never a fake screenshot.
7. **86% stat** → plain-text attribution "as reported in ODI literature (Strategyn)"; no link to
   the copyrighted in-repo PDF.

## Builder Calls (design authority — beyond the session's settled six)

1. **Formula corrected to repo truth:** the session sketch showed `Opportunity = Importance −
   Satisfaction`; the code computes `importance + max(importance − satisfaction, 0)`

2. **OG renderer = Pillow, pinned in root dev deps** (`pillow==12.3.0`, `uv.lock` updated):

   binary, deterministic bytes, zero deploy-time dependency (Pillow never ships to Pages).
   Generator also emits `favicon.png`.
3. **Full color/type/motion system specified with measured contrast ratios** (table above); palette
   lifted from the shipped Studio theme for brand continuity.
4. **Sticky compact header** (wordmark + one CTA), no nav links.
5. **`404.html` included, self-contained** — absolute home link + inline styles, because relative
   assets break when Pages serves 404.html at arbitrary depths under the `/agentic-odi/` base.
6. **Relative assets + absolute canonical/OG URLs** — required by GitHub project-Pages base path.
7. **Test/CI architecture:** `website/tests/` run by a new `website` job in `ci.yml` (added to
   `ci-green` needs) *and* as a verify-before-publish step inside the Pages deploy job; workflow
   YAML itself is contract-tested with PyYAML (`pyyaml==6.0.3` declared in root dev deps).
8. **Artifact staging** via `rsync --exclude tests/ --exclude tools/` → `_site/` (CI-only,
   gitignored): the published site is the site, nothing else.
9. **Root `[tool.ruff]` added** (line-length 100, target py310, select `E4,E7,E9,F,I,UP,B,BLE`,

11. **Closed external-link allowlist** (repo, Issues, Horizon chat, uv docs, MCP docs, canonical);

12. **No emoji on the site** (README's emoji vocabulary stays in README).
13. **Pages source toggle is a pre-merge gate**, not a post-merge note — without it `main` goes red.

Exact micro-copy polish within the binding strings above; section/illustration composition and grid
details; animation timing fine-tuning within the stated curves; favicon/mark geometry drafting within
the stated concept; breakpoint tuning; workflow YAML details not specified (names, step ordering).

## Intent & Why

contributors, wrong for the PM or eng lead who clicked a shared link asking "is this real, and is it
worth five minutes?" The site answers why/what/how/when in one scroll, with a Jobsian bar:
ruthless focus, one narrative, one obvious action, craft in type and motion, and honesty as the
brand — the project is an experimental testbed, and the page says so out loud.

one thing Jobs never did — the honest answer is the Jobsian answer.** No dates, no maturity theater,
no CTAs that dead-end behind auth, no screenshots of vaporware.

Definition of done for the build (see plan): PR pushed with all GitHub Actions checks green —
lint (ruff), typecheck (mypy), security (bandit), tests (pytest ×6 packages + `website`), smoke,

  invented Discord/Slack; access channel = GitHub Issues only.
- **No auth fiction:** local MCP config only; never link the 401 `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app`
  endpoint as something a visitor can try; no invented header/token scheme.
- **No vaporware imagery:** Studio illustration is abstraction-of-shipped-surfaces, labeled
  "Illustrative"; no fake screenshots.
- **No hotlinking `knowledge/Strategyn_*.pdf`** — attribution text only.
- **No analytics/cookies/CDN/fonts/i18n** — scope is English, one page, two schemes.
- **No publishing dev files:** `website/tests/` and `website/tools/` never reach the Pages artifact.

## Risks & Mitigations

1. **Pages not enabled before first merge** → deploy job red on `main`. Mitigation: manual toggle
   flagged as a pre-merge gate in the plan's final task.
2. **README drift** (commands/URLs change, page rots) → `test_readme_sync.py` fails CI.
3. **Committed PNG drifts from generator** → pixel-identity test fails CI until regeneration.
4. **Scope creep** (nav items, extra pages, webfonts) → anti-goals + structural tests (allowlisted
   links, weight budgets) push back mechanically.
5. **Ruff newly covers `website/**`** → root config added at repo-consistent line length; commit
   steps run root lint/format parity before every commit.

## Resolved Questions (builder-check × session — all settled)

1. **Primary CTA** → local quickstart ("Run it in 60 seconds"). Verified live: Horizon chat 302s
   to `auth.horizon.prefect.io`, hosted MCP returns 401 — a hero CTA that dead-ends anonymous
   visitors in auth is malpractice. Hosted is tertiary, labeled "requires a free Prefect account."
2. **Access channel** → GitHub Issues (footer + status section). No personal email, no invented
   Discord.
3. **MCP snippet** → local config only (`http://localhost:8000/mcp`); hosted credentials are
   requested via issues. Never document an auth scheme we don't have.
4. **OG image** → one committed PNG, regenerated by committed `website/tools/make_og.py`
   (deterministic, tested pixel-identical). SVG-only cards render poorly on X/LinkedIn/iMessage.
5. **"When"** → no dates. "What works today / What's next" under an explicit Experimental badge,
   mirroring the README roadmap.
6. **Living Studio visual** → stylized abstraction grounded in real shipped surfaces, labeled
   "Illustrative" — never a fake screenshot.
7. **86% stat** → plain-text attribution "as reported in ODI literature (Strategyn)"; no link to
   the copyrighted in-repo PDF.

## Builder Calls (design authority — beyond the session's settled six)

1. **Formula corrected to repo truth:** the session sketch showed `Opportunity = Importance −
   Satisfaction`; the code computes `importance + max(importance − satisfaction, 0)`
   (`core/src/core/models.py:28`). The page shows the real formula, and a test pins page ↔ code.
2. **OG renderer = Pillow, pinned in root dev deps** (`pillow==12.3.0`, `uv.lock` updated):
   `ImageFont.load_default(size=…)` ships the Aileron font inside Pillow — real typography, no font
   binary, deterministic bytes, zero deploy-time dependency (Pillow never ships to Pages).
   Generator also emits `favicon.png`.
3. **Full color/type/motion system specified with measured contrast ratios** (table above); palette
   lifted from the shipped Studio theme for brand continuity.
4. **Sticky compact header** (wordmark + one CTA), no nav links.
5. **`404.html` included, self-contained** — absolute home link + inline styles, because relative
   assets break when Pages serves 404.html at arbitrary depths under the `/agentic-odi/` base.
6. **Relative assets + absolute canonical/OG URLs** — required by GitHub project-Pages base path.
7. **Test/CI architecture:** `website/tests/` run by a new `website` job in `ci.yml` (added to
   `ci-green` needs) *and* as a verify-before-publish step inside the Pages deploy job; workflow
   YAML itself is contract-tested with PyYAML (`pyyaml==6.0.3` declared in root dev deps).
8. **Artifact staging** via `rsync --exclude tests/ --exclude tools/` → `_site/` (CI-only,
   gitignored): the published site is the site, nothing else.
9. **Root `[tool.ruff]` added** (line-length 100, target py310, select `E4,E7,E9,F,I,UP,B,BLE`,
   mirroring `cli/pyproject.toml`) so `website/**` Python is linted at repo standards — verified
   impact is website-only (no other root-level `.py` files exist).
10. **Hosted link = Horizon chat only**; the `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app` endpoint is never linked
    (401) — it is mentioned only as "credentials via an issue."
11. **Closed external-link allowlist** (repo, Issues, Horizon chat, uv docs, MCP docs, canonical);
    no analytics, no sitemap/robots/JSON-LD — SEO comes from meta + structure alone.
12. **No emoji on the site** (README's emoji vocabulary stays in README).
13. **Pages source toggle is a pre-merge gate**, not a post-merge note — without it `main` goes red.

## What's Left to the Builder

Exact micro-copy polish within the binding strings above; section/illustration composition and grid
details; animation timing fine-tuning within the stated curves; favicon/mark geometry drafting within
the stated concept; breakpoint tuning; workflow YAML details not specified (names, step ordering).

This is an exceptionally detailed existing spec. It explains exactly why the site looks the way it does — the "no framework" decision was made deliberately with strong reasoning ("a framework buys a toolchain, a lockfile, hydration, and an upgrade treadmill").

However, the spec was for a **single-page site in 2026-10-18**. The product has evolved 57 commits since. The spec's scope decisions ("Not a docs site, not a blog", "one page, no nav") are now stale given the user's brief: "It should contain any and all details that we need to successfully communicate to our users of our software."

So the key tension: the original spec deliberately chose minimalism/no-framework/single-page. The user now wants a state-of-the-art, Apple-grade, comprehensive site. The product itself (Living Studio) is a dark, glassy, indigo-accented chat app with 30 MCP tools, 17 connectors, a desktop app, hosted deployment.

Important: the existing spec's "no framework" reasoning was about avoiding a toolchain for a *one-page, no-routing, no-state* site. That reasoning is now weaker because:
- The site must now show much more (multi-surface, multi-page docs, real product visuals)
- The repo already has Node/Vite/React/TypeScript in apps/studio
- A framework's real payoff (component reuse, markdown-driven docs pages, code highlighting) now applies

But the counter-argument stands: GitHub Pages deploy via rsync is simple and the "no supply chain" is a real value. And the existing test contract is Python-based.

Let me now form my recommendation and ask the user the decisive questions.

Let me think about the design direction for a truly state-of-the-art site:

**The "Steve Jobs / Apple-quality" redesign direction:**

1. **Dark-first, cinematic hero** — matching the Studio's `#0a0b0e` base with the two radial indigo gradients. Full-viewport hero, huge type, an eyebrow "Experimental" pill, and a *live, interactive product surface* as the hero centerpiece (not a static image). Apple-style: one idea, one gesture.

2. **The hero should BE the product.** Instead of a screenshot, embed a real, working, interactive recreation of the Living Studio's chat surface — where you can type a customer complaint and see the agent compose an outcome-card in response. That's the "generative UI" the product is actually about. This is genuinely state-of-the-art and unique: the landing page demonstrates the product's core thesis (agent-composed surfaces from verified outcomes) rather than describing it.

   But: it must be honest. Options: (a) a scripted demo with canned responses; (b) a real call to the hosted MCP (requires sidecar — dead end); (c) a "canned but interactive" simulation. I'd recommend a **scripted interactive demo** clearly labeled as a scripted preview, with real MCP-style data — plus an honest "try it live" link.

3. **Real product surfaces as scroll-driven "lens" reveals** — the Studio's own "lens" concept: as you scroll, surfaces dock in beside the narrative.

4. **Typography-first editorial flow** — big, confident type; generous whitespace; the copy architecture from the spec but refreshed for the current product.

5. **A real docs hub** — the site should carry the CLI reference, connectors catalog, MCP tool reference, architecture, deployment, roadmap. This is the "any and all details" part. Multi-page.

6. **Code with a proper terminal aesthetic** — copy buttons that work, syntax highlighting, tabs for install paths (uv / binary / docker).

7. **Motion**: scroll-linked reveals with the Apple easings already in the Studio; respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

8. **OG/social**: regenerate with the new brand. Possibly multiple OG variants.

9. **Accessibility**: keep the AA contrast discipline the spec established, single h1, landmarks, keyboard nav.

Now, the decisions I need from the user:

**Q1: Build architecture** — static HTML (keep) vs Astro vs Vite+React.
**Q2: Scope** — single long-scroll landing vs landing + docs pages.
**Q3: Hero product demo** — scripted interactive simulation vs static render vs real API.
**Q4: Light/dark** — dark-only (matches product) vs dual theme.
**Q5: Audience priority** — dev-first vs PM-first (affects the narrative order and above-the-fold).

Let me also think about whether to use the visual companion. The brainstorming skill says to offer it just-in-time when a visual question arises. Layout/design direction IS a visual question. I should offer it when I present design options.

But wait — I'm in plan mode, and the visual companion runs a server which would be a system change (starting a background process). Hmm, plan mode says no non-readonly tools. Starting a local server is borderline. Let me not do that in plan mode; I can describe options in text and note the mockup offer for the implementation phase. Actually — the question tool lets me present side-by-side options. Let me use text.

Let me be efficient: present the findings and ask the 4-5 decisive questions in one `question` call. That's respectful of the user's time and matches "ask the user clarifying questions when weighing tradeoffs."

Let me just double-check the pages.yml and whether there's a `paths:` filter issue — the spec said `paths: [website/**, ...]` but the actual workflow (per explore) has no paths filter. Let me verify quickly, plus check ci.yml website job.

# Roadmap & Next Steps

- [x] **External MCP client connector**: Pluggable connectors package with an

  `firstRunWizard` flag.

  implementing the same `Connector` protocol.

**Answer: Everything produces static output — Pages has no runtime. The constraint is on the OUTPUT, not the tooling. Three viable paths:**

| Path | Output | Pages-safe? | npm in Pages CI? | Anti-drift? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hand-written HTML | static | ✅ | no | ❌ drifts |
| Astro | static | ✅ | yes | ❌ still needs a Python step for MCP tools |
| **Python generator → static** | static | ✅ | **no** | ✅ built-in |

**Recommendation: Python generator.** Because:
- The docs hub's reference content (30 MCP tools, CLI tree, 17 connectors, ODI schema) lives in Python/TS source. Astro/Vite would STILL need a Python extraction step and then a JSON handoff — two toolchains instead of one.
- The repo's CI is uv/pytest-based; adding Node to the Pages path means a second lockfile, a second cache, and a new supply chain for a static asset site.
- The site already has this exact proven pattern: `make_og.py` → committed `og.png` → pytest asserts pixel-identity. The same pattern scales to the whole site.
- The Studio keeps React+Vite+TS untouched. Zero change required.

**Reuse, concretely (the "bonus"):**
1. `apps/studio/src/styles/theme.css` → site tokens (one-way, no Studio change)

# Redesign Plan — Agentic ODI GitHub Pages

## 0. Answering the architecture question directly

**GitHub Pages has no runtime.** The constraint is on the *output* (static files), not the *tooling*. A build step runs in Actions, then uploads the artifact. So all three paths are Pages-legal. The real question is which produces the best result for this repo:

| Path | Output | npm in Pages CI | Anti-drift for MCP tools / CLI / connectors? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hand-written HTML | static | no | ❌ drifts immediately |
| Astro | static | yes | ❌ still needs a Python extraction step → JSON handoff |
| **Python generator → static** | static | **no** | ✅ built in |

**Recommendation: a Python static-site generator, no Node in the Pages path.** The decisive reason: the docs hub's reference content (30 MCP tools, CLI command tree, 17 connectors, ODI schema) lives in **Python source**. Astro/Vite would *still* need a Python script to extract it and then hand JSON to a second toolchain. One language, one lockfile, one CI path.

**The Studio keeps React 19 + Vite + TypeScript, untouched.** Zero required change.

This also mirrors a pattern the repo already proved: `make_og.py` → committed `og.png` → pytest asserts pixel-identity. The same pattern scales to the whole site.

 # Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails
 
 This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.
 
-> **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `knowledge/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.
+> **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `docs/reference/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.
 
 ---
 
 ## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails
 
 This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.
 
 ### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?
 
 ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.
 
 ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done
 
 - A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
 - A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
 - **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
 - ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes
 
 - **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
 - Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
 - **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):
 
   > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`
 
   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
   - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
   - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.
 
 - **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)
 
 - All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
   1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
   2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
   3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
   4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
   5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
   6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
   7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
   8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs
 
 - **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
 - ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)
 
 - Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
   - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
   - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?
 
 - **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):
 
   ```
   Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
   ```
 
 - **Interpretation**:
   - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
   - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
   - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.
 
 - **Agent rule**: Always compute and surface the opportunity score when both `importance` and `satisfaction` are provided. Highlight outcomes scoring **> 10** as the highest priority innovation targets. Use `get_outcomes(job_id)` to review the full opportunity landscape.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 5: Outcome-Based Market Segmentation
 
 - ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
 - Segments can be:
   - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
   - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
   - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value
 
 - **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.
 
 ---
 
 ### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy
 
 Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:
 
 | Strategy | When to use |
 |---|---|
 | **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
 | **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
 | **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |
 
 - **Agent rule**: When the opportunity landscape is clear (outcomes scored, segments identified), guide the user to select a strategy path and align their innovation roadmap accordingly.
 
 ---
 
 ### ⚠️ ODI Behavioral Guardrails for the Agent
 
 These are absolute constraints the agent must respect:
 
 | DO | DON'T |
 |---|---|
 | Always start by defining or confirming the Job-to-be-Done | Jump to solutions, features, or product ideas before the job is defined |
 | Guide outcome statements with the correct format | Accept vague or solution-framed statements as valid outcomes |
 | Compute opportunity scores when importance + satisfaction are available | Skip scoring or calculate it incorrectly |
 | Reference the Universal Job Map when decomposing jobs | Invent arbitrary step structures disconnected from the 8 universal stages |
 | Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments | Use demographics or assumptions to segment the market |
 | Treat outcomes as stable, measurable success metrics | Confuse outcomes with features, preferences, or solutions |
 | Call `get_odi_framework_guidelines` when stage guidance is needed | Guess at which stage comes next |

 ## 🚧 Core Development Guardrails
 
 ### 1. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Implementation
 - **Library Choice**: ALWAYS use [`fastmcp`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) for building the MCP architecture. Avoid using the lower-level Anthropic `mcp` SDK directly unless there is a hyper-specific edge case that `fastmcp` does not support.
 - **Transport Protocol**: The project is currently prototyping with **HTTP transport** (not stdio). 
   - The server should be initialized using `mcp.run(transport="http", ...)`.
   - The client must connect to the HTTP endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
 - **Tool Creation**: 
   - Register tools on the server using the `@mcp.tool` decorator.
   - **CRITICAL**: Provide comprehensive docstrings and strict Python type hints for every tool parameter. Explain exactly what the tool does and what data it expects, as this metadata is fed directly to the LLM for tool discovery.
-  - **Capability Synchronization**: Whenever you add, modify, or remove an MCP tool in `mcp_server/src/mcp_server/mcp_server.py`, you **MUST** simultaneously update the `get_capabilities` tool's human-readable return string to ensure the capability set exactly matches the code.
+  - **Contract Synchronization**: Whenever you add, modify, or remove an MCP tool in `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`, you **MUST** simultaneously update `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` (`ToolName`, `TOOL_SPECS`) and the `get_capabilities` return string. `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` enforces the surface.
 
 ### 2. Async / Client Practices
 - Use `asyncio` for client execution and IO-bound tool operations.
 - Always use the `fastmcp.Client` securely within an asynchronous context manager (`async with client:`) to ensure connections are efficiently managed and closed.
 
 ### 3. Data Schema & Persistence (ODI Domain)
 - Define all Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) entities (e.g., *Jobs*, *Steps*, *Desired Outcomes*, *Opportunity Scores*) using `pydantic` models.
 - When expanding the server to accept complex payloads or to query data, utilize these Pydantic models for built-in type validation and schema enforcement before the server processes the request.
 
 ### 4. General Philosophy
 - **Separation of Concerns**: Isolate the ODI data logic/retrieval from the MCP server tooling logic.
 - **Agentic Purpose**: Remember that the tools being built are meant to be consumed by autonomous agents. Design tool interfaces that are intuitive for an LLM to call and interpret.
-- **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `connectors/` workspace package. New kinds implement `connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
+- **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `packages/connectors` workspace package. New kinds implement `agentic_odi_connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
 - **MCP client vs ODI server**: The ODI FastMCP **server** exposes product tools. The MCP **client connector** uses `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP to ingest data from *external* MCP servers. Prefer in-memory `Client(server)` tests for that connector, same as server tests.
 
 ### 5. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
 - **First-Class Documentation**: Treat tests as living documentation that demonstrate how features work while protecting against regressions.
 - **Speed & Isolation**: Tests must be fast (< 1s) and self-contained. Use `@pytest.mark.integration` or `@pytest.mark.client_process` for slower, integration, or resource-dependent tests.
-- **Structure**: This repo is a uv workspace. Mirror each project's code structure in its own `tests/` directory (e.g., `mcp_server/src/mcp_server/mcp_server.py` -> `mcp_server/tests/test_server_tools.py`, `connectors/src/connectors/mcp/connector.py` -> `connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py`).

Mirror each project's code structure in its own `tests/` directory (e.g., `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py` -> `apps/mcp-server/tests/test_server_tools.py`, `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/mcp/connector.py` -> `packages/connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py`).
 - **Atomic Tests**: Each test must verify exactly one specific behavior with clear intent in test names and assertions. Avoid multi-behavior tests.
 - **In-Memory Testing (Preferred)**: Favor testing functionality deterministically by passing the `FastMCP` server directly into the `Client(server)` instance. This runs in-memory without network overhead for deterministic and lightning-fast execution.
 - **Transport Testing (When Needed)**: For HTTP/SSE network transport tests, prefer the isolated in-process `fastmcp.utilities.tests.run_server_async(server)` context manager over subprocess testing (which uses `run_server_in_process` and is slower to debug).
