@@ -0,0 +1,62 @@
+# Repository Architecture
+
+Agentic ODI is a uv workspace with a single root `pyproject.toml` for shared tooling. Python distributions are imported by their stable `agentic_odi_*` package names; directory layout does not leak into imports.
+
+## Layout
+
+```text
+apps/
+  cli/            agentic_odi_cli         Typer CLI: local SQLite or remote MCP
+  mcp-server/     agentic_odi_mcp_server  FastMCP server over HTTP
+  studio-api/     agentic_odi_studio_api  FastAPI sidecar for the Studio SPA
+  studio/         React + TypeScript + Vite SPA and Tauri 2 shell
+packages/
+  core/           agentic_odi_core        Domain, services, repositories, contract
+  connectors/     agentic_odi_connectors  MCP client connectors and catalog
+infra/cloudflare/ Worker + Wrangler config for the free-plan deployment
+scripts/          Dev launcher, binary build, installer checks
+tests/            Cross-package contract and launcher tests only
+docs/             Architecture, reference material, Superpowers artifacts
+packaging/        PyInstaller spec for the CLI binary
+```
+
+## Dependency Direction
+
+```text
+apps/cli ──────────────┐
+apps/mcp-server ───────┼──▶ packages/core
+apps/studio-api ───────┘         ▲
+                                 │
+apps/cli ──────────────▶ packages/connectors
+```
+
+- `packages/core` depends on no other workspace package.
+- `packages/connectors` depends on `core` only where it needs shared models.
+- Every runnable app may depend on `core`; none of them imports another app.
+- The React SPA only talks to `apps/studio-api` over `/api`; it never calls MCP or the LLM directly.
+
+## Persistence
+
+- `SQLiteRepository` is the production default for the CLI, MCP server, and Studio API.
+- The default database is `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_DB`.
+- `build_repository()` chooses SQLite by default and `InMemoryRepository` when `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:`, which is what tests use.
+- The CLI selects its backend with `--backend local|mcp` or `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND`.
+- The Studio API selects `local` (direct service calls) or `mcp` (passthrough) with `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` or `create_app(backend=...)`.
+
+## MCP Contract
+
+`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` owns `ToolName`, `ToolSpec`, `TOOL_SPECS`, and `TOOL_NAMES`. The live FastMCP registry is asserted against it by `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py`; the CLI's local handlers are checked by `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py`.
+
+## Entry Points
+
+| Command | Module |
+|---|---|
+| `agentic-odi` | `agentic_odi_cli.cli:app` |
+| `agentic-odi-server` / `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | `agentic_odi_mcp_server.mcp_server:main` |
+| `agentic-odi-studio-api` | `agentic_odi_studio_api.main:main` |
+| `uv run python scripts/dev.py` | Dev launcher (MCP + Studio API) |
+
+## Related
+
+- [Data flow](data-flow.md)
+- [Testing](testing.md)

+# Data Flow
+
+## Sources of Truth
+
+| Layer | Owns | Persists |
+|---|---|---|
+| `packages/core` | `Job`, `Step`, `Outcome`, `CustomerOutcome`, `ODIService`, repository protocol | SQLite event log + snapshots |
+| `apps/mcp-server` | MCP tool adapters over `ODIService` | `build_repository()` selects SQLite in production and in-memory for `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` |
+| `apps/studio-api` | Studio API, canvas projection, chat tool loop | Via the same repository when the local backend is active |
+| `apps/studio` | Presentation state, optimistic canvas updates | Browser cache only |
+| `apps/cli` | Terminal rendering, local/remote backend selection | SQLite directly for `local`, no local writes for `mcp` |
+
+## Write Paths
+
+### Local CLI
+
+```text
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes add
+  -> LocalBackend
+  -> ODIService
+  -> SQLiteRepository
+  -> IntentStore (append) + snapshot refresh
+```
+
+### MCP
+
+```text
+MCP client / Studio MCP mode / CLI --backend mcp
+  -> FastMCP tool
+  -> ODIService
+  -> configured Repository
+```
+
+`apps/mcp-server` builds its repository once at import time with `build_repository()`. Production uses SQLite; tests set `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` (the root test suite does this in `tests/conftest.py`).
+
+### Studio API
+
+```text
+apps/studio SPA
+  -> /api/canvas, /api/steps, /api/outcomes
+  -> backend=local: ODIService -> Repository
+  -> backend=mcp:   call_mcp_tool -> MCP server -> ODIService -> Repository
+
+apps/studio SPA
+  -> /api/chat
+  -> stream_chat -> OpenAI-compatible LLM -> MCP tool calls
+```
+
+The SPA sends `mcp_url` with every data request for compatibility. In `local` mode the sidecar ignores it; in `mcp` mode it is required for canvas and mutations.
+
+## Read Paths
+
+```text
+ODIService.get_jobs / get_job_map / get_outcomes
+  -> Repository read-through state
+  -> Pydantic models
+  -> JSON (CLI --json, MCP text payload, Studio canvas)
+```
+
+The Studio canvas falls back to the demo seed only in `mcp` mode when MCP is unreachable or returns no jobs. `local` mode returns exactly what is in the local database, including an empty canvas.
+
+## Configuration
+
+| Variable | Used by | Default |
+|---|---|---|
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | core SQLite repository | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | CLI, Studio API | `local` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | CLI, Studio defaults | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DIST` | Studio API, dev launcher | `apps/studio/dist` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT` | Tauri shell | auto-detected |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `http://localhost:8001/v1` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local-tools-model` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local` |
+
+## Trust Boundaries
+
+- The SPA runs in a browser or Tauri webview and only trusts the sidecar origin.
+- The sidecar may reach MCP and the LLM; CORS is restricted to known Studio origins.
+- MCP is an HTTP service with no authentication in local development. Do not expose it directly to the internet; the Cloudflare setup tunnels the sidecar, not MCP.

+# Testing
+
+## Commands
+
+```bash
+uv run pytest                       # all packages + root contract/launcher tests
+uv run pytest packages/core         # one package
+uv run pytest tests/contract        # MCP contract only
+uv run mypy apps packages tests
+uv run ruff check .
+uv run ruff format --check .
+uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages
+```
+
+The root `pyproject.toml` owns pytest, coverage, ruff, mypy, and bandit configuration. There is no per-package test configuration to keep in sync.
+
+## Layout
+
+Tests live next to their package (`packages/*/tests`, `apps/*/tests`). Root `tests/` contains only cross-package checks:
+
+- `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` — live FastMCP names, argument names, and required fields match `agentic_odi_core.contract.TOOL_SPECS`.
+- `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py` — the CLI local-handler keys are a subset of `TOOL_NAMES`.
+- `tests/scripts/` — dev launcher helpers and lifecycle.
+
+## Isolation Rules
+
+- Use `InMemoryRepository` in tests. `create_app(InMemoryRepository())` keeps the Studio API off the real `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`.
+- The MCP server uses `build_repository()`; tests set `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` before import and call tools through `Client(mcp)` without HTTP.
+- Async tests use `@pytest.mark.asyncio` (strict mode).
+
+## Coverage
+
+CI runs the root suite on Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12, collects coverage for every `agentic_odi_*` distribution, and uploads `coverage.xml` from the 3.12 job. Codecov requires 90% project coverage; patch coverage is advisory. Python tests and `apps/studio/**` are excluded from the report by `codecov.yml`.
+
+## Frontend
+
+```bash
+npm --prefix apps/studio run lint
+npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck
+npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run
+npm --prefix apps/studio run build
+cd apps/studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check
+```

@@ -0,0 +1,224 @@
+# CLI Reference
+
+The `agentic-odi` CLI is a [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based
+command-line interface for working with Agentic ODI without a chat UI. It
+provides an interactive chat mode plus version, update, and data commands. Data
+commands are **local-first**: they read and write a SQLite store with no server
+required, and switch to a remote MCP server with `--backend mcp`.
+
+Install the workspace first if you have not already:
+
+```bash
+uv sync --all-packages
+```
+
+## Launching
+
+```bash
+python -m agentic_odi_cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
+python -m agentic_odi_cli --help      # show available options and commands
+python -m agentic_odi_cli             # start interactive chat in a terminal (help when piped)
+```
+
+A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way.
+
+## Global options
+
+| Option | Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `--backend local\|mcp` | `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | `local` | Run in-process against SQLite, or call a remote MCP server. |
+| `--db PATH` | `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` | Store path for the `local` backend. |
+| `--mcp-url URL` | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | Server URL for the `mcp` backend. |
+
+Data commands print readable tables and blocks by default; add `--json` for
+machine-readable output. Diagnostics go to stderr and failures exit non-zero
+(`0` success, `1` error, `2` usage error).
+
+## Interactive chat
+
+`agentic-odi chat` (or simply `agentic-odi` in a terminal) starts an
+offline-first interactive REPL. The session always boots, even when no model or
+MCP server is reachable — a yellow warning is shown for any unavailable service,
+and free-text messages return a friendly nudge until you connect.
+
+```bash
+agentic-odi chat
+agentic-odi chat --model local-tools-model --mcp-url http://localhost:8000/mcp
+```
+
+### Connection settings
+
+The chat resolves settings in priority order:
+**CLI flag → environment variable → persisted profile → built-in default.**
+
+| Variable | Default | CLI flag |
+|---|---|---|
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | `--base-url` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | `--model` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | `--api-key` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | `--mcp-url` |
+
+The **persisted profile** is stored at
+`~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json`. You can create or update it from
+within the session using `/connect`.
+
+### Slash commands
+
+| Command | Description |
+|---|---|
+| `/help` | Show all available commands |
+| `/status` | Show current model, base URL, and MCP server with connection status |
+| `/connect` | Launch the wizard: provider → URL → API key → model → MCP URL → save |
+| `/model <name>` | Hot-swap to a different model mid-session |
+| `/mcp <url>` | Reconnect to a different MCP server mid-session |
+| `/tools` | List the MCP tools the assistant can call |
+| `/clear` | Reset conversation history (keeps connection) |
+| `/exit` | Quit the session (also `/quit`) |
+
+### /connect wizard
+
+`/connect` walks you through configuring your LLM provider interactively:
+
+1. **Provider** — choose `openai`, `anthropic`, `local`, or `other`
+2. **Base URL** — preset filled for known providers; override freely
+3. **API key** — input is hidden via `getpass`
+4. **Model** — sensible default per provider
+5. **MCP URL** — defaults to the current value
+6. **Save to profile?** — writes `~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json` so settings persist across sessions
+
+The wizard can be cancelled at any step with Ctrl-C.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Chat is the only CLI mode that needs an LLM endpoint. The `customer-outcomes`
+> and `connectors` commands keep working without one.
+
+## Manage Jobs, Steps, and desired Outcomes
+
+Every ODI entity has the same create/read/update/delete surface in the CLI and
+the MCP server. Jobs hold Steps (the Job Map) and desired Outcomes; deleting a
+Job cascades to both.
+
+```bash
+# Jobs
+agentic-odi jobs add --name "Onboard a customer" --description "First 30 days"
+agentic-odi jobs list
+agentic-odi jobs get <job-id>
+agentic-odi jobs update <job-id> --name "Onboard a new customer"
+agentic-odi jobs delete <job-id> --yes
+
+# Steps (Job Map)
+agentic-odi steps add --job-id <job-id> --name "Prepare environment" --order 1
+agentic-odi steps list --job-id <job-id>
+agentic-odi steps get <step-id>
+agentic-odi steps update <step-id> --order 2
+agentic-odi steps delete <step-id> --yes
+
+# Desired Outcomes
+agentic-odi desired-outcomes add --job-id <job-id>   --statement "Minimize the time it takes to get a working environment"   --importance 8 --satisfaction 4
+agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
+agentic-odi desired-outcomes get <outcome-id>
+agentic-odi desired-outcomes update <outcome-id> --satisfaction 6
+agentic-odi desired-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
+```
+
+Add `--json` to any command for machine-readable output.
+
+## Evidence
+
+Evidence is research captured from connectors (or entered by hand) and linked to
+a Job, Step, or desired Outcome. Records can later be promoted into ODI
+artifacts — the bridge from research to the model, without hand-copying.
+
+```bash
+# Capture a record by hand
+agentic-odi evidence add \
+  --source-name "interview" --source-kind manual \
+  --name "Support lead" \
+  --content "Setup takes two days for every new engineer" \
+  --job-id <job-id>
+
+# Read and delete
+agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id>
+agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id> --json
+agentic-odi evidence get <evidence-id>
+agentic-odi evidence delete <evidence-id> --yes
+
+# Promote into the ODI model
+agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to job
+agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to outcome --job-id <job-id>
+```
+
+`connectors ingest --job-id <job-id>` maps every evidence-bearing record in the
+ingested batch into evidence in one step.
+
+## Schema and scoring
+
+```bash
+agentic-odi schema            # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity
+agentic-odi score 8 2         # ODI opportunity score → 14.00
+```
+
+## Manage Customer Outcomes
+
+Customer Outcomes link customer value to business value. The `local` backend
+writes to the shared SQLite store with no server required; add `--backend mcp`
+to route through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). The group is also
+available under its historical name `outcomes`.
+
+```bash
+# Add a Customer Outcome
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
+  --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
+  --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
+  --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 \
+  --category cost_reduction \
+  --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"
+
+# Attach value metrics: repeatable JSON objects
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
+  --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
+  --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
+  --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction \
+  --business-statement "Saves engineering hours" \
+  --value-metric '{"name":"first response","direction":"minimize","unit_of_measure":"minutes","importance":7,"satisfaction":3}'
+
+# List outcomes (optionally filtered, or as JSON)
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes list
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --json
+
+# Get, update, delete
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes get <outcome-id>
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
+
+# Compute an ODI Opportunity Score (top-level, also under the group)
+agentic-odi score 8 2
+agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
+```
+
+`score` applies the ODI opportunity formula,
+`importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`.
+
+Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` (or `--mcp-url`) to point to a non-default server when
+using `--backend mcp` (default: `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
+
+## Connectors
+
+The `connectors` group manages external MCP integrations. See
+[External Connectors](connectors.md) for presets, the connector registry, and
+ingest behavior.
+
+```bash
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset github
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors list
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors health --name github
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors ingest --name github
+```
+
+## Updates
+
+`odi update` checks for and installs a new binary release. Auto-update is on by
+default; disable it with `--no-update` for one run or
+`AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1` globally. See [Installation](installation.md).

+# External Connectors (MCP Ingest)
+
+Connectors are named integrations stored in `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` (or a
+path you pass with `--config` / `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE`). The first kind is
+`mcp`: Agentic ODI acts as an MCP **client** and pulls catalog, resources, and
+optional tool results from an external MCP **server**.
+
+## Presets
+
+The fastest way to connect is a preset. `connectors catalog` lists every
+built-in preset, grouped by the capability area it serves:
+
+```bash
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog                          # all presets
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog --area strategy-alignment
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog --json
+```
+
+| Capability area (`--area`) | Presets |
+|---|---|
+| Voice of customer & qualitative research (`voice-of-customer`) | `notion`, `gong`, `fireflies`, `intercom`, `confluence` |
+| Quantitative data & opportunity scoring (`quantitative-data`) | `posthog`, `amplitude`, `mixpanel` |
+| Market & competitive intelligence (`market-intelligence`) | `exa`, `tavily` |
+| Product strategy & backlog alignment (`strategy-alignment`) | `linear`, `github`, `jira`, `miro`, `figma` |
+| Strategy & knowledge management output (`knowledge-output`) | `slack` |
+
+Register one with `--preset`; `--name` defaults to the preset id:
+
+```bash
+# Token-based preset: export the variable it needs first
+export GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=ghp_...
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset github
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors health --name github
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors ingest --name github
+
+# OAuth-based preset: the browser consent flow starts on first use
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset notion
+```
+
+Credentials never enter the registry. Presets that use API keys store `${VAR}`
+placeholders that are resolved from the environment when a connection is
+opened, and `connectors health` names any variable that is missing. `--url`
+overrides the endpoint (self-hosted or proxied deployments) and `--tool` still
+selects which tools to call during ingest.
+
+Custom servers keep working the same way:
+
+```bash
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --name internal --url https://mcp.internal.example/mcp --tool latest_quote
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors list
+```
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Presets cover MCP servers with a hosted endpoint. Servers you run yourself
+> (Snowflake, BigQuery, Google Drive, Brave Search, and similar) are added with
+> an explicit `--url`. The catalog lives in
+> `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/catalog.py`.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> OAuth tokens are cached in memory for the life of one CLI process, so an OAuth
+> preset may ask for consent again on the next `connectors health` or
+> `connectors ingest`. Prefer a token-based preset where the server offers one.
+
+## Ingest behavior
+
+Ingested records are normalized (`catalog`, `resource`, `tool_result`) and
+appended to the in-process ingest sink. They are **not** written into the ODI
+jobs/outcomes store — mapping ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts is still on
+the [roadmap](roadmap.md).
+
+Additional kinds (REST, webhooks, and so on) can register against the same
+`Connector` protocol later.

@@ -0,0 +1,140 @@
+# Deployment
+
+## Project Site (GitHub Pages)
+
+The static site in `website/` is published to
+**[https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)**
+by [`.github/workflows/pages.yml`](../.github/workflows/pages.yml).
+
+- A push to `main` runs the website tests, builds `_site` from `website/`, and
+  deploys the artifact with `actions/deploy-pages`.
+- `workflow_dispatch` republishes the site from the Actions tab without a code
+  change.
+- Pages is configured with the "GitHub Actions" source, so there is no
+  `gh-pages` branch. Removing `pages.yml` stops all publishing and the site
+  returns 404.
+- The `github-pages` environment only allows deployments from `main`.
+
+## Hosted MCP Server
+
+The server is deployed via **[Horizon Prefect](https://www.prefect.io/horizon)**,
+Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents.
+
+## Test Chat (UI)
+
+Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser:
+
+> **[https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat](https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat)**
+
+## MCP Server Endpoint
+
+Integrate via the MCP protocol at:
+
+> **[https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp](https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp)**
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> **Authentication is required** to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach
+> out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a
+> client.
+
+## Hosted Studio
+
+The Living Studio SPA is deployed to Cloudflare Workers:
+
+| Environment | URL |
+|---|---|
+| Production (`main`) | **[https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)** |
+| Pull request preview | Posted automatically by Cloudflare Workers Builds as a PR comment |
+
+Production deploys on every push to `main`. The Worker is `agentic-odi`; keep
+`name` in `wrangler.jsonc` aligned with the Worker connected in the dashboard.
+Preview builds run for non-production branches and are ephemeral: the Cloudflare
+PR comment is the source of truth, so do not copy a preview URL into docs. The
+hosted UI loads without a backend; canvas data, chat, and mutations need the
+sidecar tunnel described below.
+
+## Living Studio on a Free Cloudflare Worker
+
+Workers Containers — the only way to run the Python sidecar entirely on
+Cloudflare — requires the Workers Paid plan. On the free plan, the Worker serves
+the built SPA as Workers Static Assets and proxies `/api/*` to the sidecar
+through a free, account-less
+[Cloudflare Quick Tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/get-started/quick-tunnels/).
+
+`wrangler.jsonc` publishes `apps/studio/dist` with SPA fallback and runs the Worker
+first for `/api/*`; `infra/cloudflare/worker.ts` forwards those calls to the
+`SIDECAR_URL` secret. The browser only talks to the Worker origin, so the
+sidecar's CORS list is not involved.
+
+```bash
+# 1. Build the SPA that the Worker uploads as static assets
+npm --prefix apps/studio ci
+npm --prefix apps/studio run build
+
+# 2. Terminal A — MCP server (:8000) + sidecar (:8100)
+python scripts/dev.py
+
+# 3. Terminal B — free public URL for the sidecar (no account required)
+cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8100
+# copy the https://<random>.trycloudflare.com URL it prints
+
+# 4. Store the URL on the Worker, then deploy
+npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL   # paste the trycloudflare URL
+npx wrangler deploy
+```
+
+Workers Builds settings (Workers & Pages → your Worker → Settings → Builds):
+
+| Setting | Value |
+|---|---|
+| Production branch | `main` |
+| Root directory | `/` |
+| Build command | `npm --prefix apps/studio ci && npm --prefix apps/studio run build` |
+| Deploy command | `npx wrangler deploy` |
+| Preview command | `npx wrangler preview` |
+
+A Worker has no run command: the Worker script runs on Cloudflare. Set `name` in
+`wrangler.jsonc` to the Worker you created before the first deploy.
+
+### Pull request previews
+
+Workers Builds posts the build status and Preview URL to the pull request
+automatically. To enable it:
+
+1. Open the Worker → **Settings** → **Build** → **Branch control**.
+2. Keep the production branch set to `main` and enable **Preview Builds**.
+3. If Cloudflare shows **Set up Worker Previews**, complete the one-time switch.
+   This cannot be reversed.
+4. Confirm the Preview command is `npx wrangler preview`.
+
+`wrangler.jsonc` must keep a `previews` block, even an empty one: the
+`wrangler preview` command fails the build with "Your Wrangler configuration is
+missing a `previews` block" without it. Assets and compatibility settings stay
+at the top level, so `"previews": {}` is enough while Previews need no extra
+settings. If a future Preview needs vars or bindings, add them under `previews`
+with Preview-safe values.
+
+Previews do not inherit production settings. The SPA loads from a Preview, but
+`/api/*` returns `502 SIDECAR_URL is not configured` until a preview-specific
+`SIDECAR_URL` secret is configured:
+
+```bash
+npx wrangler preview secret put SIDECAR_URL --name <branch>
+```
+
+When `--name` is omitted it defaults to the current git branch. Previews are
+ephemeral, and pull requests from forks may not receive one. If Cloudflare does
+not comment, paste the URL into the PR's **Deployment** section.
+
+The `cf` CLI can inspect build triggers and recent builds (`cf builds triggers
+list`, `cf builds list`) and create a Preview (`cf previews deploy`), but it does
+not post GitHub PR comments. The Workers Builds Git integration owns the PR link;
+`cf` is only an optional verification tool and requires `cf auth login`.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> The sidecar runs on your machine, so the Worker only works while
+> `python scripts/dev.py` and the Quick Tunnel are running. Quick Tunnel URLs
+> change on every restart — update the secret with
+> `npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL`. Chat also needs a reachable
+> OpenAI-compatible endpoint in the Studio's **Settings**; the canvas, job map,
+> and impact simulation work without one.

+# Development
+
+Everything below mirrors what CI runs. Install the workspace first:
+
+```bash
+uv sync --all-packages
+```
+
+## Linting, Formatting & Type Checks
+
+Shared tooling lives in the root `pyproject.toml`, so one command covers every
+Python project:
+
+```bash
+uv run ruff check .
+uv run ruff format --check .
+uv run mypy apps packages
+uv run --directory website mypy .
+
+# Security scanning
+uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages website/
+```
+
+## Frontend & Desktop Checks (studio)
+
+The SPA and Tauri shell mirror their CI jobs locally:
+
+```bash
+npm --prefix apps/studio run lint       # ESLint
+npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck  # tsc --noEmit
+npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run  # Vitest (run once)
+npm --prefix apps/studio run build      # production build → apps/studio/dist
+cd apps/studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check
+```
+
+### Conversational UI coverage
+
+The agent-composed surfaces and the first-run tour are covered at these levels:
+
+| File | What it covers |
+|---|---|
+| `apps/studio/src/ui/protocol.test.ts` | Spec parsing: prop types, enums, ranges, required props, depth/node/size ceilings, unknown types |
+| `apps/studio/src/ui/UiRenderer.test.tsx` | Card rendering, computed opportunity scores, action dispatch, per-node failure isolation, catalog/registry parity |
+| `apps/studio/src/components/chat/Conversation.test.tsx` | Prose and surfaces interleaved in the agent's order; card actions become messages |
+| `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_ui_spec.py` | Catalog validation and `render_ui` tool-schema generation |
+| `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_chat_ui.py` | `render_ui` interception, `ui` SSE events, and the correction fed back to the model |
+| `apps/studio/src/features/flags.test.ts` | Flag precedence (query → storage → env → default), value parsing, local overrides |
+| `apps/studio/src/onboarding/machine.test.ts` | Tour transitions, no forward motion without a goal, versioned storage, malformed records |
+| `apps/studio/src/onboarding/FirstRunWizard.test.tsx` | Auto-open, full flow to a destination, skip/Escape, focus trap, resume, replay, inline model repair, flag off |
+| `apps/studio/src/App.test.tsx` | First-run ordering: tour over the context conversation, job handoff, chosen surface opens, flag off in shell tests |
+
+## Website Checks (GitHub Pages)
+
+The `website/` static site is part of the main CI workflow. Its tests assert the
+committed OG art is reproducible, that `index.html` stays in sync with the
+README, and that the publish pipeline (`website/tests/test_pages_deploy.py`)
+still exists:
+
+```bash
+uv run --directory website pytest tests/
+```
+
+Publishing happens in `.github/workflows/pages.yml`: it runs those tests, builds
+`_site` from `website/`, and deploys the artifact with `actions/deploy-pages` on
+every push to `main`. There is no `gh-pages` branch, so that workflow is the only
+thing that keeps <https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/> online.
+
+## Formatting workflow
+
+- **When editing Python files**, either rely on the **pre-commit hooks** below
+  (recommended) or run Ruff formatting directly before pushing:
+
+  ```bash
+  uv run ruff format .
+  ```
+
+- **CI behavior**:
+  - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files.
+  - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only.
+  - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the
+    changes, and push again.
+
+## Pre-commit hooks
+
+To run the checks automatically before each commit:
+
+```bash
+uv tool install pre-commit
+pre-commit install
+```
+
+After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` run on staged files whenever you commit.
+You can also trigger them manually:
+
+```bash
+pre-commit run --all-files
+```
+
+## Testing
+
+Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely
+in-memory — no running server required. Tests live next to the package they
+cover, and every test runs from the repository root:
+
+```bash
+uv run pytest                        # everything
+uv run pytest apps/cli               # one app
+uv run pytest packages/core          # one package
+uv run pytest tests/contract         # cross-package contracts
+uv run pytest tests/scripts          # dev launcher
+```
+
+The MCP server contract test compares the live FastMCP registry with
+`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py`, so add or change a tool in
+both places. The CLI local-backend contract test keeps `_LOCAL_HANDLERS` aligned
+with the same tool names.
+
+## Test Coverage
+
+CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and uploads one combined
+`coverage.xml` from the 3.12 job to
+[Codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi).
+
+The Codecov upload authenticates with the `CODECOV_TOKEN` repository secret and
+is non-blocking (`fail_ci_if_error: false`), so a Codecov outage or a fork PR
+without secrets cannot fail the test job. The badge at the top of the README
+tracks `main`, which is the baseline every PR is compared against:
+
+- **Project** status requires at least **90%** coverage (`target: 90%`) and
+  tolerates a 1% dip from `codecov.yml`.
+- **Patch** status is informational for now, so new code can land while the
+  suite catches up.
+
+To reproduce the report locally:
+
+```bash
+uv run pytest \
+  --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
+  --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
+  --cov=agentic_odi_core \
+  --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
+  --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
+  --cov-report=term-missing \
+  --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml
+```
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Coverage is only collected for the Python packages. `apps/studio/` and test
+> directories are excluded in `codecov.yml`.
+
+### Conventions
+
+- Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named
+  `test_*.py`.
+- Root `tests/` is reserved for cross-package checks (`contract/` and
+  `scripts/`).
+- Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`.
+- Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests.
+- The MCP server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before
+  each test.
+
+### Test Coverage Map
+
+| Area | What it covers |
+|---|---|
+| `packages/core/tests/` | Domain models, opportunity scoring, `ODIService`, repository implementations, SQLite persistence, schema, and repository factory |
+| `apps/mcp-server/tests/` | Full ODI workflow, entity parity, context tools, Customer Outcomes, evidence, tool errors, and HTTP transport startup |
+| `apps/studio-api/tests/` | Health, config, canvas, SSE chat, SPA fallback, MCP hydration, probes, and step/outcome passthrough |
+| `apps/cli/tests/` | Backend selection, local/remote CRUD, chat, wizard, onboarding, updates, rendering, connectors, and startup performance |
+| `packages/connectors/tests/` | Catalog presets, registry persistence, factory, MCP and REST connectors, evidence mapping, and sink |
+| `tests/contract/` | Live MCP tool surface and CLI local-handler parity |
+| `tests/scripts/` | `scripts/dev.py` startup, port checks, signals, and shutdown |
+| `apps/studio/src/**/*.test.ts` | SPA units: ODI math, transport bridge, SSE parser, sidecar client |
+| `website/tests/` | Static site integrity, OG art reproducibility, and README sync |
+
+> [!TIP]
+> Type `/test` in the AI assistant to have the agent run all tests and report the
+> results automatically.
+
+## Agent Session Tracking
+
+Agent sessions are captured with the [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview)
+CLI. The repository integration lives in `.entire/settings.json`,
+`.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. Run `entire status` to
+confirm it is enabled and `entire checkpoint list` to inspect captured
+checkpoints.

+# Installation
+
+Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Install the latest
+release with one command:
+
+```bash
+curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
+```
+
+The installer places the binary under `~/.local/share/agentic-odi/versions/<version>/`,
+creates a `current` symlink, and symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and
+`agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`.
+
+If `~/.local/bin` is not on your PATH, add it (e.g.,
+`export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`). On Windows, the PowerShell installer
+uses `~\AppData\Local\agentic-odi\` and copies `.exe` files to
+`~\AppData\Local\agentic-odi\bin\`.
+
+## Update
+
+By default, `odi` auto-checks for updates once every 24 hours and applies the
+update on the next run (auto-update is enabled by default). Control behavior
+with:
+
+- `odi update` — explicit check and update
+- `--no-update` flag — skip auto-update for this run
+- `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1` — disable auto-update globally
+
+When running from a non-frozen source install, auto-update is suppressed
+automatically.
+
+## Install layout
+
+```text
+~/.local/share/agentic-odi/
+  ├── versions/<version>/
+  │   └── odi (and bundled files)
+  └── current -> versions/<version>
+
+~/.local/bin/
+  ├── odi -> ../share/agentic-odi/current/odi
+  ├── odipm
+  ├── odi-cli
+  └── agentic-odi
+
+~/.config/agentic-odi/  # state/preferences
+```
+
+Environment variables: `AGENTIC_ODI_INSTALL_DIR` (override install root),
+`XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_BIN_HOME`. The default backend is `local`
+(`--backend local`); no MCP server is required.
+
+## Unsigned binaries
+
+macOS may quarantine downloaded binaries:
+`xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ~/.local/bin/odi` (if needed). Windows SmartScreen
+may show a warning for unsigned binaries; choose "More info → Run anyway" if you
+trust the release.
+
+## Release automation
+
+Releases are cut and published by CI with no approval step:
+
+1. Conventional commits land on `main`; `release-please` opens or updates the
+   release PR.
+2. The `release-please` workflow arms auto-merge on that PR. `main` requires the
+   `CI green` check (ruleset `main-requires-ci-green`), so the PR merges itself
+   as soon as CI passes — nobody clicks merge.
+3. The merge cuts tag `vX.Y.Z` and the GitHub Release; the tag starts the
+   `release` and `Tauri Release` workflows, which attach the CLI archives,
+   `checksums.txt`, the install scripts, and the desktop bundles to it.
+   The `release-instructions` job then appends an end-user "## 📦 Download &
+   Run" section to the release page, listing the per-platform archives,
+   `checksums.txt`, and the install scripts, plus one-line install and
+   quick-run commands (idempotent on re-runs).
+4. `e2e-install` runs after `release` succeeds and installs the published binary
+   on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
+
+**One-time setup (GitHub App).** GitHub holds workflow runs that start from
+`GITHUB_TOKEN`-authored pushes ("This workflow requires approval from a
+maintainer") and ignores the tag such a push creates, which is why releases used
+to need a maintainer. A release-only GitHub App avoids both:
+
+1. Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → New GitHub App, with
+   permissions: Contents `Read and write`, Issues `Read and write`, Pull
+   requests `Read and write` (no webhook).
+2. Install the App on this repository.
+3. Add repository secrets `RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID` (the App's client ID)
+   and `RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` (a generated private key).
+
+Until those secrets exist, the `release-please` workflow logs a warning and falls
+back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`: releases still happen, but the release PR needs a
+maintainer approval and merge, and the tag will not start the asset builds. After
+adding the secrets, re-run the workflow (`gh workflow run release-please.yml`) or
+push to `main` so the open release PR is re-driven by the App.
+
+To check the installer without cutting a release, run
+`bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh` — it serves a simulated release over HTTP and
+exercises `scripts/install.sh` end to end (CI runs it too).

+
+| Source | Example | Use |
+|---|---|---|

+| Default | on | |
+
+Accepted values are `1`/`0`, `true`/`false`, `on`/`off`, `yes`/`no`, and
+`enabled`/`disabled`. With the flag off, no dialog renders, no onboarding state
+is written, and Settings hides the replay action.
+
+### Guidance, not gates
+
+The setup conversation is a nudge, never a prerequisite. If you skip it, the
+home stage keeps a dashed **Tell me what you're building** pill; it reopens the
+conversation exactly where you left off. `/start` and Settings do the same. The conversation also understands a
+natural reply: say "skip", "not now", or "show me the landscape" and it reacts
+instead of recording it as an answer. When a brief exists, it opens on a review
+and asks what changed rather than asking everything again.
+
+### Without a model
+
+When the LLM is unreachable the Studio keeps working:
+
+- A **Working by hand** strip explains the state and offers capture, job map,
+  and context.
+- Messages still return deterministic ODI guidance from the sidecar, labelled
+  **Local guidance**.
+- Jobs can be created, renamed, and deleted; steps added, edited, and removed;
+  outcomes recorded, re-scored, and removed. All of it goes through the same
+  local repository the model uses.
+- Settings → Base URL and Model reconnect the assistant whenever you are ready.
+
+The user's context is sent with every chat request, so the assistant starts from
+the product, audience, job, and problem rather than asking for them again.
+
+### The thread is the room
+
+Capture, scoring, simulation, and decisions are conversations. The storefront
+never asks the PM to leave the thread to do work: the agent asks for the
+customer's words or the bet in plain language, then renders the surface that
+carries it. A lens exists for reading and for people who prefer a click, not for
+doing the work.
+
+That is also enforced in the agent's system prompt: it is told to keep every
+artifact in the conversation, never to send the PM to a panel, and to end each
+reply with the next move as an action on the surface.
+
+## Rich responses
+
+The copilot does not only talk. When a surface carries the evidence better than a
+paragraph, the agent renders one **inline in the conversation**: a scored
+outcome, a ranked opportunity board, a before/after simulation of a bet, a
+customer quote with its lineage, the eight-stage job map, or a decision record.
+Three properties keep this safe and cheap to extend:
+
+- **The catalog is closed and owned by the SPA.**
+  `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` declares nine primitives and six cards, their
+  JSON Schema props, and the description the model reads. There is no HTML, no
+  eval, and no third-party component in the path. Prose is rendered by the same
+  `Markdown` component the transcript already used.
+- **The sidecar is catalog-agnostic.** The SPA sends the catalog with each turn;
+  the sidecar derives the `render_ui` tool schema from it, validates what comes
+  back, and streams a `ui` SSE event. Invalid props return to the model as a tool
+  result naming the exact violation, and the loop offers the tool again, so a
+  fumbled prop is corrected in the same reply. A client that sends no catalog
+  never sees the tool.
+- **Cards are views, never actors.** Every button is an `intent` string that the
+  agent receives as the user's next message — one authority, one audit trail.
+
+A surface is one node tree, streamed as one event:
+
+```json
+{
+  "type": "outcome-card",
+  "props": {
+    "id": "O-1",
+    "statement": "Minimize the time it takes to propagate secrets across environments",
+    "importance": 9,
+    "satisfaction": 3
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The conversation keeps the order the agent produced: a `delta` appends to the
+open prose part, a `ui` event opens a card, and the next `delta` opens a new
+paragraph after it. The opportunity score is computed from importance and
+satisfaction when the agent omits it, so the ODI formula has exactly one home
+(`src/lib/odi.ts`). Unknown component types degrade to a quiet fallback; a tree
+that fails validation is dropped whole, and the surrounding prose still reads.
+
+### Adding a surface
+
+1. Add an entry to `CATALOG` in `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` — props as a
+   JSON Schema subset, plus the description the model will read.
+2. Register the component in `apps/studio/src/ui/registry.ts`.
+3. Implement it in `apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx` (domain shape) or
+   `apps/studio/src/ui/primitives.tsx` (composition).
+4. Run `npm --prefix apps/studio test`. The `registry parity` test fails if the
+   catalog and the registry drift apart.
+
+No server change is needed, and no new dependency.

+## Hosted (experimental)
+
+The built SPA is also served from Cloudflare Workers at
+**[https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**.
+The UI loads without a backend; canvas data, chat, and mutations need the local
+sidecar and MCP server. Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers
+Builds. See [Deployment](deployment.md) for the Worker setup.

+## 1. Web — production build (recommended for a quick look)

+```bash

+|---|---|
+| MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp |
+| Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 |

+stop both.

+## 2. Web — dev with hot reload

+# open http://localhost:5173

+The app spawns the MCP server and sidecar itself:

+```bash

+## Desktop signing & updater secrets

+Self-updating and code signing are **env-driven**: if a secret is absent, an
+unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub
+Actions secrets.

+|---|---|

+| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password for the private key (optional when the key has none). |
+| `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` / `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 `.p12`) and its password. |
+| `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | macOS signing identity. |
+| `APPLE_ID` / `APPLE_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | macOS notarization credentials. |
+| `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` / `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config. |

+# Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend
+
+To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a
+local LLM backend that:
+
+- Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example,
+  `/v1/chat/completions`), and
+- Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**.
+
+A simple fully local option is
+[`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run
+a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server.
+
+## 1. Install a local LLM server
+
+Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for
+platform-specific build notes):
+
+```bash
+pip install llama-cpp-python
+```
+
+## 2. Download a small tools-capable model
+
+Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a
+7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g.
+`C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`.
+
+## 3. Start the OpenAI-compatible server
+
+Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default
+used by the Living Studio sidecar and the CLI chat:
+
+```bash
+python -m llama_cpp.server \
+  --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \
+  --model_alias local-tools-model \
+  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \
+  --chat_format openai
+```
+
+This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`.
+
+## 4. Configure the Studio
+
+The Living Studio sidecar and the CLI chat read the following environment
+variables (with sensible defaults):
+
+| Variable | Default |
+|---|---|
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` |
+| `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` |
+
+You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Living Studio's
+**Settings** panel.
+
+## 5. Verify tool-calling against the MCP server
+
+- (Optional) Before starting the UI, confirm the LLM backend is reachable:
+
+  ```bash
+  curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models
+  ```
+
+  If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before
+  debugging the MCP client/server.
+
+- Start the MCP server and Studio (via `python scripts/dev.py` or one of the
+  [run modes](living-studio.md)).
+- In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for
+  example: *"Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI
+  repository."*
+- You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for
+  example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI
+  guidance, confirming the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work
+  together.
+- If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI shows a clear error
+  banner indicating the configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with
+  details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps
+  above to fix your local LLM setup.

+# Superpowers (Pi, OpenCode & Freebuff)
+
+This project includes [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) as a
+[Pi package](https://pi.dev/docs/packages). When using [Pi](https://pi.dev) with
+this project, Superpowers skills and extensions are automatically loaded.
+
+## Enable with Pi
+
+1. Install Pi: `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh`
+2. Trust the project (first time only): `pi config --local --approve`
+3. Start Pi: `pi`
+
+The `.pi/settings.json` declares the Superpowers package. Pi clones it and loads:
+
+- **Extension**: `superpowers.ts` — injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at
+  session startup and after compaction
+- **Skills**: 12 Superpowers skills (TDD, subagent-driven-development,
+  systematic-debugging, etc.)
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Superpowers is also available for OpenCode via the plugin in `opencode.json`.
+> The Pi package provides native Pi integration without needing the OpenCode
+> compatibility layer.
+
+## Freebuff
+
+This project ships [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) for
+[Freebuff](https://freebuff.com) as repo-local skills plus a session-start
+bootstrap. No plugin or hook is required:
+
+- **Skills**: `.agents/skills/` contains 15 Superpowers skills. Freebuff
+  discovers them automatically; load one with the `skill` tool.
+- **Bootstrap**: `AGENTS.md` injects the `using-superpowers` rules and the
+  Freebuff tool mapping at session start.
+- **Mapping**: `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/freebuff-tools.md`
+  maps skill actions to Freebuff tools.
+
+Start Freebuff in the repository and ask "What are your superpowers?" to verify.
+See [docs/superpowers/freebuff-setup.md](superpowers/freebuff-setup.md) for
+update and troubleshooting notes.

+"""Ready-to-use MCP connector presets for common ODI workflows.
+
+Each preset captures everything needed to register a connector for a well-known
+MCP server: the endpoint, how it authenticates, and where its documentation
+lives. Presets are grouped by the five capability areas an outcome-driven
+innovation process needs, so a new workspace can be wired up with
+``agentic-odi connectors add mcp --preset <id>`` instead of hunting for URLs.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import ConnectorConfig
+
+CapabilityArea = Literal[
+    "voice-of-customer",
+    "quantitative-data",
+    "market-intelligence",
+    "strategy-alignment",
+    "knowledge-output",
+]
+
+AREA_LABELS: dict[CapabilityArea, str] = {
+    "voice-of-customer": "Voice of customer & qualitative research",
+    "quantitative-data": "Quantitative data & opportunity scoring",
+    "market-intelligence": "Market & competitive intelligence",
+    "strategy-alignment": "Product strategy & backlog alignment",
+    "knowledge-output": "Strategy & knowledge management output",
+}
+
+ENV_VAR_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}")
+
+
+class UnknownPresetError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, preset_id: str) -> None:
+        self.preset_id = preset_id
+        super().__init__(f"Unknown preset: {preset_id} (try 'agentic-odi connectors catalog')")
+
+
+class UnknownAreaError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, area: str) -> None:
+        self.area = area
+        valid = ", ".join(AREA_LABELS)
+        super().__init__(f"Unknown capability area: {area} (expected one of: {valid})")
+
+
+class ConnectorPreset(BaseModel):
+    """A known MCP server plus the credentials it needs."""
+
+    id: str
+    label: str
+    area: CapabilityArea
+    summary: str
+    url: str
+    auth: Literal["none", "oauth"] = "none"
+    env_vars: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    headers: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    docs: str
+    tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    is_recommended: bool = False
+
+    def referenced_env_vars(self) -> set[str]:
+        """Environment variables the URL or headers interpolate with ``${VAR}``."""
+        found: set[str] = set()
+        for value in [self.url, *self.headers.values()]:
+            found.update(ENV_VAR_PATTERN.findall(value))
+        return found
+
+
+PRESETS: tuple[ConnectorPreset, ...] = (
+    # 1. Voice of customer & qualitative research
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="notion",
+        label="Notion",
+        is_recommended=True,
+        area="voice-of-customer",
+        summary="Interview notes, feedback logs, and PRDs from Notion pages.",
+        url="https://mcp.notion.com/mcp",
+        auth="oauth",
+        docs="https://developers.notion.com/docs/mcp",
+    ),
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="gong",
+        label="Gong",
+        area="voice-of-customer",
+        summary="Sales and success call transcripts with direct customer quotes.",
+        url="https://mcp.gong.io/mcp",
+        auth="oauth",
+        docs="https://help.gong.io/",
+    ),
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="fireflies",
+        label="Fireflies.ai",
+        area="voice-of-customer",
+        summary="Meeting transcripts and summaries for unmet-need mining.",
+        url="https://mcp.fireflies.ai/mcp",
+        auth="oauth",
+        docs="https://docs.fireflies.ai/",
+    ),
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="intercom",

+        if area not in AREA_LABELS:

+    if recommended:
+        presets = [preset for preset in presets if preset.is_recommended]
+    return presets

+def get_preset(preset_id: str) -> ConnectorPreset:
+    for preset in PRESETS:

+    preset: ConnectorPreset,
+    *,
+    name: str | None = None,
+    url: str | None = None,
+    tools: list[str] | None = None,
+    enabled: bool = True,

+    """Build a registry entry from a preset, allowing local overrides."""
+    settings: dict[str, Any] = {
+        "url": url or preset.url,
+        "auth": preset.auth,
+        "headers": dict(preset.headers),
+        "env_vars": list(preset.env_vars),
+        "tools": list(tools if tools is not None else preset.tools),
+    }

+        name=name or preset.id,
+        kind="mcp",

+"""Kind registry that maps connector configs onto Connector implementations."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.mcp.connector import MCPClientConnector
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import (
+    ConnectorConfig,
+    McpConnectorSettings,
+    RestConnectorSettings,
+)
+from agentic_odi_connectors.protocol import Connector
+from agentic_odi_connectors.registry import UnknownConnectorKindError
+from agentic_odi_connectors.rest.connector import RestConnector, WebhookConnector
+
+Builder = Callable[[ConnectorConfig], Connector]
+
+_builders: dict[str, Builder] = {}
+
+
+def register_kind(kind: str, builder: Builder) -> None:
+    """Register a builder for a connector kind (mcp today; others later)."""
+    _builders[kind] = builder
+
+
+def known_kinds() -> set[str]:
+    return set(_builders)
+
+
+def build_connector(config: ConnectorConfig) -> Connector:
+    try:
+        builder = _builders[config.kind]
+    except KeyError:
+        raise UnknownConnectorKindError(config.kind) from None
+    return builder(config)
+
+
+def _build_mcp(config: ConnectorConfig) -> Connector:
+    settings = McpConnectorSettings.model_validate(config.settings)
+    return MCPClientConnector(name=config.name, settings=settings)
+
+
+def _build_rest(config: ConnectorConfig) -> Connector:
+    settings = RestConnectorSettings.model_validate(config.settings)
+    return RestConnector(name=config.name, settings=settings)
+
+
+def _build_webhook(config: ConnectorConfig) -> Connector:
+    settings = RestConnectorSettings.model_validate(config.settings)
+    return WebhookConnector(name=config.name, settings=settings, kind="webhook")
+
+
+register_kind("mcp", _build_mcp)
+register_kind("rest", _build_rest)
+register_kind("webhook", _build_webhook)

+"""Map connector ingest records onto ODI evidence drafts.
+
+This module deliberately does not import the ODI store. It produces transport
+records shaped for ``core.Evidence``; the CLI (or any caller) owns persistence,
+so connector plumbing never leaks into the ODI repository.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import EvidenceItemType, IngestBatch, IngestRecord
+
+
+class EvidenceDraft(BaseModel):
+    """An ingest record ready to become ODI evidence."""
+
+    source_name: str
+    source_kind: str
+    item_type: EvidenceItemType
+    name: str
+    content: str
+    raw: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    job_id: str | None = None
+    step_id: str | None = None
+    outcome_id: str | None = None
+
+
+def drafts_from_batch(
+    batch: IngestBatch,
+    *,
+    job_id: str | None = None,
+    step_id: str | None = None,
+    outcome_id: str | None = None,
+    include_catalog: bool = False,
+) -> list[EvidenceDraft]:
+    """Turn every evidence-bearing record in ``batch`` into a draft.
+
+    Catalog records describe the connector itself and are skipped unless
+    ``include_catalog`` is set.
+    """
+    drafts: list[EvidenceDraft] = []
+    for record in batch.records:
+        if record.item_type == "catalog" and not include_catalog:
+            continue
+        drafts.append(_draft_from_record(record, job_id, step_id, outcome_id))
+    return drafts
+
+
+def _draft_from_record(
+    record: IngestRecord,
+    job_id: str | None,
+    step_id: str | None,
+    outcome_id: str | None,
+) -> EvidenceDraft:
+    return EvidenceDraft(
+        source_name=record.source_name,
+        source_kind=record.source_kind,
+        item_type=record.item_type,
+        name=record.name,
+        content=record.content,
+        raw=record.raw,
+        job_id=job_id,
+        step_id=step_id,
+        outcome_id=outcome_id,
+    )

--- packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/mcp/connector.py

@@ -0,0 +1,176 @@
+"""MCP client connector that ingests tools and resources from an external server."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import os
+import re
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from typing import Any
+
+from fastmcp import Client, FastMCP
+from fastmcp.client.transports import StreamableHttpTransport
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import (
+    HealthStatus,
+    IngestBatch,
+    IngestRecord,
+    McpConnectorSettings,
+)
+from agentic_odi_connectors.protocol import Connector
+
+_ENV_VAR_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}")
+
+
+class MissingEnvironmentError(RuntimeError):
+    """Raised when a connector needs credentials that are not in the environment."""
+
+    def __init__(self, names: list[str]) -> None:
+        self.names = names
+        super().__init__("Missing environment variable(s): " + ", ".join(names))
+
+
+def _expand_env(value: str, environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> str:
+    return _ENV_VAR_PATTERN.sub(lambda match: environ.get(match.group(1), ""), value)
+
+
+def _to_dict(obj: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    if hasattr(obj, "model_dump"):
+        dumped = obj.model_dump(mode="json")
+        if isinstance(dumped, dict):
+            return dumped
+    return {"repr": repr(obj)}
+
+
+def _content_text(obj: Any) -> str:
+    parts: list[str] = []
+    content = getattr(obj, "content", None)
+    if content is None:
+        text = getattr(obj, "text", None)
+        return text if isinstance(text, str) else json.dumps(_to_dict(obj))
+    for item in content:
+        text = getattr(item, "text", None)
+        if isinstance(text, str):
+            parts.append(text)
+    return "\n".join(parts) if parts else json.dumps(_to_dict(obj))
+
+
+class MCPClientConnector(Connector):
+    """Pulls catalog, resources, and optional tool results from an MCP server."""
+
+    kind = "mcp"
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        name: str,
+        settings: McpConnectorSettings,
+        *,
+        server: FastMCP | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        self.settings = settings
+        self._server = server
+
+    def transport(self) -> StreamableHttpTransport | FastMCP:
+        """Build the MCP transport, resolving credentials from the environment."""
+        if self._server is not None:
+            return self._server
+        missing = sorted(name for name in self.settings.env_vars if not os.environ.get(name))
+        if missing:
+            raise MissingEnvironmentError(missing)
+        headers = {
+            key: _expand_env(value, os.environ) for key, value in self.settings.headers.items()
+        }
+        return StreamableHttpTransport(
+            url=_expand_env(self.settings.url, os.environ),
+            headers=headers or None,
+            auth="oauth" if self.settings.auth == "oauth" else None,
+        )
+
+    def _client(self) -> Client:
+        return Client(self.transport())
+
+    async def health(self) -> HealthStatus:
+        try:
+            async with self._client() as client:
+                tools = await client.list_tools()
+                resources = await client.list_resources()
+            return HealthStatus(
+                ok=True,
+                message="reachable",
+                details={
+                    "tool_count": len(tools),
+                    "resource_count": len(resources),
+                },
+            )
+        except MissingEnvironmentError as exc:
+            return HealthStatus(
+                ok=False,
+                message=str(exc),
+                details={"missing_env": exc.names},
+            )
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            return HealthStatus(ok=False, message=str(exc))
+
+    async def ingest(self) -> IngestBatch:
+        batch = IngestBatch(connector_name=self.name)
+        try:
+            async with self._client() as client:
+                tools = await client.list_tools()
+                resources = await client.list_resources()
+                tool_dicts = [_to_dict(tool) for tool in tools]
+                resource_dicts = [_to_dict(resource) for resource in resources]
+                catalog_raw = {"tools": tool_dicts, "resources": resource_dicts}
+                batch.records.append(
+                    IngestRecord(
+                        source_name=self.name,
+                        source_kind=self.kind,
+                        item_type="catalog",
+                        name="mcp-catalog",
+                        content=json.dumps(catalog_raw, indent=2),
+                        raw=catalog_raw,
+                    )
+                )
+                for resource in resources:
+                    uri = str(getattr(resource, "uri", ""))
+                    name = str(getattr(resource, "name", None) or uri)
+                    try:
+                        contents = await client.read_resource(uri)
+                        content_text = "\n".join(
+                            getattr(item, "text", "") or "" for item in contents
+                        )
+                        batch.records.append(
+                            IngestRecord(
+                                source_name=self.name,
+                                source_kind=self.kind,
+                                item_type="resource",
+                                name=name,
+                                content=content_text,
+                                raw={"uri": uri, "resource": _to_dict(resource)},
+                            )
+                        )
+                    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+                        batch.errors.append(f"Failed to read resource {uri}: {exc}")
+                configured_tools = self.settings.tools
+                available = {str(getattr(tool, "name", "")) for tool in tools}
+                for tool_name in configured_tools:
+                    if tool_name not in available:
+                        batch.errors.append(f"Tool not found: {tool_name}")
+                        continue
+                    try:
+                        result = await client.call_tool(tool_name, {})
+                        batch.records.append(
+                            IngestRecord(
+                                source_name=self.name,
+                                source_kind=self.kind,
+                                item_type="tool_result",
+                                name=tool_name,
+                                content=_content_text(result),
+                                raw={"tool": tool_name, "result": _to_dict(result)},
+                            )
+                        )
+                    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+                        batch.errors.append(f"Failed to call tool {tool_name}: {exc}")
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            batch.errors.append(str(exc))
+        return batch

+"""Shared Pydantic models for external connectors and ingest records."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import uuid
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+ItemType = Literal["resource", "tool_result", "catalog"]
+McpAuthMode = Literal["none", "oauth"]
+EvidenceItemType = Literal["catalog", "resource", "tool_result", "manual", "note"]
+
+
+class HealthStatus(BaseModel):
+    ok: bool
+    message: str
+    details: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+
+
+class IngestRecord(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    source_name: str
+    source_kind: str
+    item_type: ItemType
+    name: str
+    content: str
+    raw: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+
+
+class IngestBatch(BaseModel):
+    connector_name: str
+    records: list[IngestRecord] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    errors: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+class McpConnectorSettings(BaseModel):
+    """Connection details for an MCP server.
+
+    ``url`` and ``headers`` may interpolate environment variables with
+    ``${VAR}`` so registry files never hold tokens. ``env_vars`` names the
+    variables that must be present before connecting.
+    """
+
+    url: str
+    tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    auth: McpAuthMode = "none"
+    headers: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    env_vars: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+class RestConnectorSettings(BaseModel):
+    url: str
+    method: Literal["GET", "POST"] = "GET"
+    headers: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    json_body: dict[str, Any] | None = None
+    records_key: str | None = None
+    timeout: float = 10.0
+    item_type: ItemType = "resource"
+
+
+class ConnectorConfig(BaseModel):
+    name: str
+    kind: str
+    enabled: bool = True
+    settings: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

+"""Resolve the shared connector configuration file path.
+
+The path is shared by the CLI, the Living Studio sidecar, and the MCP
+ingest connector so every entry point reads and writes the same
+``connectors.json``. An explicit override is honored via the
+``AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`` environment variable; otherwise the
+config lives under the user's platform config directory.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+
+CONFIG_PATH_ENV = "AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG"
+
+
+def config_path() -> Path:
+    """Return the path to the shared ``connectors.json`` registry file."""
+    env = os.getenv(CONFIG_PATH_ENV)
+    if env:
+        return Path(env)
+    return Path.home() / ".config" / "agentic-odi" / "connectors.json"
+
+
+__all__ = ["CONFIG_PATH_ENV", "config_path"]

+"""JSON-backed registry of named connector configurations."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import ConnectorConfig
+
+
+class UnknownConnectorKindError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, kind: str) -> None:
+        self.kind = kind
+        super().__init__(f"Unknown connector kind: {kind}")
+
+
+class DuplicateConnectorError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        super().__init__(f"Connector already exists: {name}")
+
+
+class ConnectorNotFoundError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        super().__init__(f"Connector not found: {name}")
+
+
+def _known_kinds() -> set[str]:
+    from agentic_odi_connectors.factory import known_kinds
+
+    return known_kinds()
+
+
+class ConnectorRegistry:
+    """Persists connector configs to a JSON file."""
+
+    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
+        self.path = path
+
+    def add(self, config: ConnectorConfig) -> None:
+        if config.kind not in _known_kinds():
+            raise UnknownConnectorKindError(config.kind)
+        connectors = self._load()
+        if any(existing.name == config.name for existing in connectors):
+            raise DuplicateConnectorError(config.name)
+        connectors.append(config)
+        self._save(connectors)
+
+    def list_all(self) -> list[ConnectorConfig]:
+        return self._load()
+
+    def get(self, name: str) -> ConnectorConfig:
+        for config in self._load():
+            if config.name == name:
+                return config
+        raise ConnectorNotFoundError(name)
+
+    def delete(self, name: str) -> bool:
+        connectors = self._load()
+        kept = [config for config in connectors if config.name != name]
+        if len(kept) == len(connectors):
+            raise ConnectorNotFoundError(name)
+        self._save(kept)
+        return True
+
+    def _load(self) -> list[ConnectorConfig]:
+        if not self.path.exists():
+            return []
+        with self.path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            payload: dict[str, Any] = json.load(handle)
+        raw_connectors = payload.get("connectors", [])
+        return [ConnectorConfig.model_validate(item) for item in raw_connectors]
+
+    def _save(self, connectors: list[ConnectorConfig]) -> None:
+        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        payload = {"connectors": [item.model_dump(mode="json") for item in connectors]}
+        with self.path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            json.dump(payload, handle, indent=2)
+            handle.write("\n")

+"""REST and webhook connector kinds.
+
+Both kinds share one HTTP puller: a REST endpoint returns a JSON document, and a
+webhook connector posts a configured request (usually to a webhook inbox or a
+subscription endpoint) and normalizes the JSON response. The transport is
+injectable so tests never touch the network.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import urllib.request
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from typing import Any
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import (
+    HealthStatus,
+    IngestBatch,
+    IngestRecord,
+    RestConnectorSettings,
+)
+from agentic_odi_connectors.protocol import Connector
+
+FetchResult = tuple[int, bytes]
+Fetcher = Callable[[str, str, dict[str, str], bytes | None, float], FetchResult]
+
+
+def _default_fetch(
+    method: str,
+    url: str,
+    headers: dict[str, str],
+    body: bytes | None,
+    timeout: float,
+) -> FetchResult:
+    request = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, headers=headers, method=method)
+    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:  # nosec B310
+        return int(response.status), response.read()
+
+
+def _lookup(payload: Any, path: str) -> Any:
+    current = payload
+    for part in path.split("."):
+        if not isinstance(current, dict) or part not in current:
+            return None
+        current = current[part]
+    return current
+
+
+class RestConnector(Connector):
+    """Pulls JSON records from an HTTP endpoint into the ingest sink."""
+
+    kind = "rest"
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        name: str,
+        settings: RestConnectorSettings,
+        *,
+        kind: str | None = None,
+        fetcher: Fetcher | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        self.settings = settings
+        self.kind = kind or type(self).kind
+        self._fetch = fetcher or _default_fetch
+
+    def _request(self) -> FetchResult:
+        body = None
+        headers = dict(self.settings.headers)
+        if self.settings.json_body is not None:
+            body = json.dumps(self.settings.json_body).encode("utf-8")
+            headers.setdefault("Content-Type", "application/json")
+        return self._fetch(
+            self.settings.method,
+            self.settings.url,
+            headers,
+            body,
+            self.settings.timeout,
+        )
+
+    def _items(self, payload: Any) -> list[Any]:
+        if self.settings.records_key:
+            extracted = _lookup(payload, self.settings.records_key)
+            if isinstance(extracted, list):
+                return extracted
+        if isinstance(payload, list):
+            return payload
+        if isinstance(payload, dict):
+            for key in ("records", "items", "data"):
+                value = payload.get(key)
+                if isinstance(value, list):
+                    return value
+        return [payload]
+
+    def _record(self, item: Any, index: int) -> IngestRecord:
+        if isinstance(item, dict):
+            name = str(
+                item.get("name")
+                or item.get("title")
+                or item.get("id")
+                or f"{self.name}-{index + 1}"
+            )
+            content = None
+            for key in ("content", "text", "description", "body", "summary"):
+                if isinstance(item.get(key), str):
+                    content = item[key]
+                    break
+            if content is None:
+                content = json.dumps(item, indent=2, default=str)
+            raw = item
+        elif isinstance(item, str):
+            name = f"{self.name}-{index + 1}"
+            content = item
+            raw = {"value": item}
+        else:
+            name = f"{self.name}-{index + 1}"
+            content = json.dumps(item, default=str)
+            raw = {"value": item}
+        return IngestRecord(
+            source_name=self.name,
+            source_kind=self.kind,
+            item_type=self.settings.item_type,
+            name=name,
+            content=content,
+            raw=raw,
+        )
+
+    async def health(self) -> HealthStatus:
+        try:
+            status, _ = self._request()
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            return HealthStatus(ok=False, message=str(exc))
+        ok = 200 <= status < 400
+        return HealthStatus(
+            ok=ok,
+            message="reachable" if ok else f"HTTP {status}",
+            details={"status": status, "url": self.settings.url},
+        )
+
+    async def ingest(self) -> IngestBatch:
+        batch = IngestBatch(connector_name=self.name)
+        try:
+            status, body = self._request()
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            batch.errors.append(str(exc))
+            return batch
+        if not 200 <= status < 400:
+            batch.errors.append(f"HTTP {status} from {self.settings.url}")
+            return batch
+        text = body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+        try:
+            payload: Any = json.loads(text)
+        except json.JSONDecodeError:
+            payload = text
+        records = self._items(payload)
+        for index, item in enumerate(records):
+            batch.records.append(self._record(item, index))
+        return batch
+
+
+class WebhookConnector(RestConnector):
+    """Posts to a webhook endpoint and ingests the JSON response."""
+
+    kind = "webhook"

+"""In-memory ingest sink owned by the connectors package."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import IngestBatch, IngestRecord
+
+
+class IngestSink:
+    """Stores ingested batches for the current process."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._batches: list[IngestBatch] = []
+
+    def append(self, batch: IngestBatch) -> None:
+        self._batches.append(batch)
+
+    def batches(self) -> list[IngestBatch]:
+        return list(self._batches)
+
+    def records(self) -> list[IngestRecord]:
+        return [record for batch in self._batches for record in batch.records]
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        self._batches.clear()
+
+
+_default_sink = IngestSink()
+
+
+def get_default_sink() -> IngestSink:
+    return _default_sink

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import RestConnectorSettings
+from agentic_odi_connectors.rest.connector import RestConnector, WebhookConnector
+
+Calls = list[tuple[str, str, dict[str, str], bytes | None, float]]
+
+
+def _fetcher(status: int, payload: Any, calls: Calls | None = None):
+    def fetch(
+        method: str, url: str, headers: dict[str, str], body: bytes | None, timeout: float
+    ) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
+        if calls is not None:
+            calls.append((method, url, headers, body, timeout))
+        text = payload if isinstance(payload, str) else json.dumps(payload)
+        return status, text.encode("utf-8")
+
+    return fetch
+
+
+def _connector(payload: Any, status: int = 200, **settings: Any) -> RestConnector:
+    base: dict[str, Any] = {"url": "https://api.example/records"}
+    base.update(settings)
+    return RestConnector(
+        name="jira",
+        settings=RestConnectorSettings(**base),
+        fetcher=_fetcher(status, payload),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_health_reports_reachable_on_2xx() -> None:
+    status = await _connector([]).health()
+
+    assert status.ok is True
+    assert status.message == "reachable"
+    assert status.details["status"] == 200
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_health_reports_http_failure() -> None:
+    status = await _connector([], status=503).health()
+
+    assert status.ok is False
+    assert "503" in status.message
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_ingest_normalizes_list_payload() -> None:
+    batch = await _connector([{"name": "ticket-1", "content": "Login fails"}]).ingest()
+
+    assert batch.errors == []
+    assert len(batch.records) == 1
+    record = batch.records[0]
+    assert record.name == "ticket-1"
+    assert record.content == "Login fails"
+    assert record.source_name == "jira"
+    assert record.source_kind == "rest"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_ingest_uses_records_key_and_serializes_objects() -> None:
+    payload = {"result": {"issues": [{"id": "ABC-1", "summary": "Slow deploy"}]}}
+    batch = await _connector(payload, records_key="result.issues").ingest()
+
+    assert len(batch.records) == 1
+    assert batch.records[0].name == "ABC-1"
+    assert batch.records[0].content == "Slow deploy"
+    assert batch.records[0].raw["id"] == "ABC-1"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_ingest_treats_plain_text_as_one_record() -> None:
+    batch = await _connector("customer says onboarding is slow").ingest()
+
+    assert len(batch.records) == 1
+    assert batch.records[0].content == "customer says onboarding is slow"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_ingest_records_fetch_errors() -> None:
+    def fetch(*_args: Any) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
+        raise ConnectionError("refused")
+
+    connector = RestConnector(
+        name="jira",
+        settings=RestConnectorSettings(url="https://api.example/records"),
+        fetcher=fetch,
+    )
+
+    batch = await connector.ingest()

+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_webhook_posts_json_body_and_uses_configured_item_type() -> None:
+    calls: Calls = []
+    connector = WebhookConnector(
+        name="inbox",
+        settings=RestConnectorSettings(
+            url="https://hooks.example/inbox",
+            method="POST",
+            json_body={"query": "latest"},
+            item_type="tool_result",
